13.2. `spells.2da` projectile presentation and `progfx.2da` MIRV runtime are linked, not equivalent.
   - A `spells.2da` projectile family (`Proj`, `ProjModel`, `ProjType`, `ProjSpwnPoint`, `ProjSound`, `ProjOrientation`, `HasProjectile`) creates an `AuroraSpellProjectilePresentationRequest` or equivalent. It is a spell/action presentation lane with caster/target/timing policy, not a `visualeffects.2da` phase and not a parsed `progfx.2da` row.
   - A `progfx.2da` Type 10/11 MIRV/projectile row is a phase-owned programmed-FX runtime request. It is reachable only from an owning `visualeffects.2da` `ProgFX_Impact`, `ProgFX_Duration`, or `ProgFX_Cessation` field after the row has a selected EE/profile source. The same projectile model token can therefore appear in two different owner lanes and must keep the owner edge.
   - When a Type 10/11 programmed row points at a `spells.2da` line or spell/projectile payload, create an explicit bridge record such as `AuroraSpellProjectileProgFxBridge`. Minimum fields: owning `visualeffects.2da` row and phase field path, selected `progfx.2da` row/type/raw params, linked `spells.2da` row/source layer, spell projectile fields, caster/source object, target object/location, call mode (`realSpell`, `fakeSpell`, item-property spell, unknown), and selected runtime profile.
   - `ImpactScript`, `BardImpactScript`, and `MirvImpactScript` stay script refs on the spell/action lane. They can inform validation policy, but they never become model resources, VFX row resources, MDL emitter chunks, or `progfx.2da` params.
   - Fake-cast paths need an explicit visual-only policy. External Lexicon evidence says fake spell actions reuse casting/projectile visuals from the selected spell row but do not fire the spell script, so a fake-cast bridge must not schedule impact-script-created VFX, AOE, damage, or MIRV payloads unless a separate scripted/runtime event proves them.
   - Cache keys must preserve the lane split. A spell projectile presentation key includes spell row, source profile, projectile fields, caster/target, call mode, and timing policy. A programmed-MIRV key additionally includes owning VFX row, phase field path, `progfx` row/type/raw params, effect-instance context, selected transform/miss data, and profile. A row-only key can replay the wrong projectile path, spawn anchor, fake-vs-real policy, or MIRV phase.
   - Local Aurora evidence proves `spells` table bootstrap and spell/toolset projectile vocabulary, while this export still does not expose a `progfx` table string or a recovered MIRV constructor body. Treat the bridge as an implementation safety contract that combines local source authority with EE/external profile evidence, not as local decompilation proof of every MIRV branch.

15. VFX source/resource resolver contract.
   - Use the shared resolver boundary from `resolver-interfaces-contract-r69.md`: request, candidate catalog, policy evaluation, trace, winner, diagnostics, and policy version.
   - VFX must not do ad hoc `rg`/filename scans in typed readers. Every table, model, texture, TXI, MTR, shader, chunk MDL, sound, and dependent `spells.2da` lookup needs source provenance.
   - The current `ResourceType` contract has `ARE`, `GIT`, `2DA`, `TLK`, `UTC`, `UTP`, and `OTHER`. VFX should either extend this enum with typed model/texture/material/shader/sound classes or carry an explicit `requestedResourceClass` whenever `OTHER` is used.
   - Minimum VFX resolve request fields: raw token, normalized lookup key, requested resource class, candidate extensions/resource types, source table/row/column or emitter field path, runtime profile, source layer policy, and whether the dependency is required for canonical preview.
   - Resource classes are distinct even when the raw token text is identical:
     - `2da`: `visualeffects`, `progfx`, `iprp_visualfx`, `spells`, and profile-specific support tables.
     - `model`: impact/cessation MDLs, `chunkName`, ProgFX model params, projectile models, Type 12 node-attached VFX models.
     - `texture`: emitter `texture`, TXI texture directives, MTR `texture0..texture10`, envmap/bump/specular/procedural refs, and PLT/TPC/DDS/TGA candidates.
     - `material`: MTR sidecars and explicit `materialname` refs.
     - `shader`: Aurora particle/beam-volume shader names and MTR custom shader refs.
     - `sound`: impact/duration/cessation sounds and ProgFX sound params.
   - Resolver output must be an edge graph, not just a flat list:
     - `visualeffects.2da row -> phase slot -> MDL model resource`
     - `MDL model -> node emitter -> emitter texture resource`
     - `MDL model -> node emitter -> chunkName MDL resource`
     - `MDL mesh -> materialname -> MTR resource`
     - `MTR -> texture0..texture10 -> texture resources`
     - `MTR -> customShaderVS/FS/GS -> SHD resources`
     - `texture -> same-name TXI sidecar`
     - `ProgFX row -> typed Param* -> model/texture/sound/spell/beam dependency`
   - Each edge needs parent resource identity, parent source field path, requested resource class, allowed extensions/resource types, selected source layer, runtime profile, whether it is canonical runtime input or preview/sidecar metadata, and diagnostics.
   - `materialname` and `texture0` are material/mesh-lane inputs; emitter `texture` is a particle-texture lane input; `chunkName` is a spawned-model lane input. Do not flatten them into one "texture dependency" list.
   - MTR custom shaders and `renderhint` are material-lane metadata. The recovered particle draw path starts on `vsparticle`/`fsparticle`, then can call a material helper after particle-shader binding; preserve that optional material-program rebind candidate instead of assuming material shader data drives particle update math or emitter `blend` parsing.
   - TXI directives can affect texture loading/metadata, alpha mean, procedural/animation hints, or sampling, but they are still sidecar texture metadata. They must not rewrite MDL emitter `update`, `render`, `blend`, atlas frame stepping, particle lifetime, or active/free list behavior.
   - EE-specific PLT, MTR, custom shader, and VFX spawned-model fog/self-illumination behavior is profile-gated. Classic/Aurora profiles preserve these references but must not silently implement EE renderer changes.
   - Project policy currently records `module_decompiled -> module_packed -> hak -> override -> vanilla KEY/BIF` for models/textures/2DA/TLK, with 2DA/TLK specs often omitting `override` in the shortened chain. Keep the policy ID/version in every VFX resolver result.
   - Community NWN resource-order docs say HAK resources can override module resources and that HAK order matters. This may conflict with project R65 for some resource classes. Aurora-first implementation must not hide that gap: record the selected project policy, emit a runtime-precedence-validation diagnostic for HAK/module conflicts, and compare against the retail client before claiming exact resource parity.
   - Once a winning `visualeffects.2da` or `progfx.2da` file is selected, do not merge missing rows or cells from lower-precedence files. Preserve lower-precedence availability only as trace data.
   - Preserve raw resrefs before normalization. NWN1/EE resrefs are 16-character runtime names in external API evidence, while current repo helper normalization sometimes allows longer internal IDs; VFX must not truncate before diagnostics and profile-aware lookup.
   - Local Aurora evidence has `CExoResMan`, `CResRef`, `CResHelper<CRes2DA,2017>`, `CResHelper<CResTXI,2022>`, `CResHelper<CResDDS,2033>`, `CResHelper<CResMTR,2072>`, `CResTGA`, `CAuroraTXI`, `CAuroraMTR`, HAK resource classes, and ResMan not-found logging. This supports a typed resource resolver, not string-only file matching.

16. Source-row lifecycle and effect-instance key contract.
   - Source row ID is the physical `visualeffects.2da` row after valid 2DA parsing. The displayed first-column token is provenance, not the only authoritative row ID.
   - External NWN Wiki evidence says `visualeffects.2da` line IDs are network-limited to a `uint16_t`/WORD range in NWN:EE. Implementation should diagnose out-of-profile row IDs before building runtime references.
   - Source row resolution produces an `AuroraVfxSourceRow`, but not a runnable effect by itself.
   - A runnable VFX instance is created only after adding:
     - constructed effect kind (`visualEffect`, `beam`, item-property visual, programmed-FX adapter, or unknown)
     - application mode (`object`, `location`, temporary duration, permanent duration, instant client play, persistent/AOE path)
     - selected phase (`impact`, `duration`, `cessation`, programmed subphase)
     - target object/location and target model/node context
     - EE transform tuple and miss flag when present
     - beam source object and body-node context when present
   - Do not cache renderer output only by `visualeffects.2da` row ID. Same row ID with different effect kind, phase, target, transform, miss flag, or beam body node can produce different visual output or validity diagnostics.
   - Model/emitter resource assets may be cached by resolved resource refs, but effect-instance scheduling and attachment state must remain per-instance.
   - Local spell/toolset strings such as `fxground`, `fximpact`, `fxhead`, `fxbeam`, `fxfail`, `conjurevisual`, and `castvisual` are upstream slots. They can eventually resolve to VFX rows, but they are not `visualeffects.2da` columns and do not define particle behavior.
   - `C:\Projects\New Folder\export\strings.tsv:15797-15814`
   - External row-limit source: https://nwn.wiki/spaces/NWN1/pages/38174875/2da%2BFiles

16.1. `progfx.2da` source rows add programmed-effect context, but they still do not become standalone emitters.
   - `ProgFX_Impact`, `ProgFX_Duration`, and `ProgFX_Cessation` must be stored as phase refs on the owning `visualeffects.2da` row. They are not interchangeable with `Imp_*`/`Ces_*` model slots, `Sound*` slots, MDL `node emitter` rows, or Blender particle settings.
   - A selected `progfx.2da` source row must carry the table-loading profile (`clientLoaded`, `serverLoaded`, `toolsetLoaded`) and row-limit profile used to admit it. Missing table-profile evidence emits diagnostics before any typed programmed-FX behavior is exposed.
   - A `progfx.2da` row without an owning `visualeffects.2da` row ID and one of the exact phase field paths is source-table data only. It cannot be scheduled, previewed as canonical, or used as an `EffectVisualEffect` row by itself.
   - A resolved `progfx.2da` row creates an `AuroraProgrammedFxSourceRow` with `type`, `params[]`, `phase`, source/provenance, and unresolved-resource diagnostics; it does not by itself provide the effect target, source object, beam body node, duration, transform, miss flag, or object node namespace.
   - Type 7/beam-style rows require an effect-instance beam context before any canonical preview. A visualeffects row with `Type_FD = B` is still not the same thing as MDL emitter `render Beam`.
   - Type 10/MIRV rows require source/target object context and projectile timing validation; `dm_visualeffect` alone is not sufficient because the documented command path does not cover source-object-dependent VFX reliably.
   - Type 12/model-node rows must resolve the named target node in the target model namespace. Missing target nodes must stay diagnostic output, not guessed anchors.
   - Any `progfx.2da` row that spawns or attaches an MDL model must route through the spawned-model mesh/material/fog lane, not the textured-particle quad lane.
   - Because `progfx` is absent from the local decompilation export, future implementation must tag `progfx` behavior as `eeExternal`/profile evidence until a matching Aurora/EE branch or retail capture confirms it.

16.2. Programmed FX require a runtime request layer, not just a parsed row.
   - The parser should produce `AuroraProgrammedFxSourceRow`; the effect builder should produce a separate `AuroraProgrammedFxRuntimeRequest`. The request must carry the owning `visualeffects.2da` row ID/source layer, the exact phase field path (`ProgFX_Impact`, `ProgFX_Duration`, or `ProgFX_Cessation`), resolved `progfx.2da` row ID, `Type`, raw `Param1..Param8`, constructed effect kind, application mode, duration mode, target/location choice, miss flag, EE transform tuple, creator/source object provenance, beam context, attachment namespace, and evidence profile.
   - The only canonical entry point from source tables into `AuroraProgrammedFxRuntimeRequest` is the owning `visualeffects.2da` phase ref plus effect-instance context. Direct `progfx.2da` row preview is a preserve/diagnostic path, not a scheduler.
   - The typed payload should include `paramOwner = progfx.2da`/source-row provenance or equivalent. A `Param1` value copied from item-property GFF/property parsing is a schema collision, not a valid programmed-FX parameter.
   - Typed interpretation is a two-stage parse: preserve raw params first, then expose a typed view only through the `Type` discriminator and only when the selected schema/profile has evidence. There must be no global `Param1`/`Param2` meaning shared across all programmed FX.
   - The `Type` column is authoritative for dispatch. Numeric row buckets, labels, or old hardcoded-family ranges may be useful diagnostics, but they cannot override `Type` when the row is parsed from a profile-gated `progfx.2da`.
   - Type 1 damage-chunk programmed FX keep nested `visualeffects.2da` row references as VFX row dependencies. They are not MDL `chunkName` emitters, and they need cycle protection if a nested row resolves back to the parent row or phase.
   - Type 3/static glow and Type 6/pulsing aura are overlay/material candidates, not particle-quads by default. Their typed payload needs target-material/creature-equipment context before canonical browser rendering.
   - Type 4 light/vision requests are a client-light/perception lane. A Three.js point light can only be preview metadata unless retail capture proves the priority/proximity/vision semantics.
   - Type 7 beam requests consume explicit `EffectBeam` context when available and record fallback/generic beam context when created through `EffectVisualEffect`; neither path becomes MDL emitter `render Beam`.
   - Type 10/11 MIRV/projectile requests require source object, target object/location, spell/projectile edge provenance, travel/orientation/path tokens, and timing evidence. A row-only preview must remain unsupported/preserve-only.
   - When Type 10/11 references a `spells.2da` row or spell projectile payload, the runtime request must attach a spell/projectile bridge rather than copying spell columns into `progfx` params. Missing spell context is a runtime-request diagnostic, not permission to render a generic emitter from the projectile model.
   - Fake-cast and real-spell call modes are separate context values for Type 10/11 bridge requests because fake spell actions can show projectile/casting visuals while suppressing `ImpactScript` execution.
   - Type 12 model-node VFX requests require a target model-node namespace, a resolved target node, and a spawned-model lane for the attached VFX model. A missing node is diagnostic output, not a fallback to model origin, hand, head, or beam BODY_NODE.
   - Type 8, Type 9, and Type 13 are preserve-only until a retail capture or EE branch decomp proves exact behavior. Delete/unload, hardcoded chunk/gib, and freeze-animation semantics are too stateful to synthesize from row text.
   - Cache keys must include owning VFX row, phase field path, `progfx` row ID, `Type`, raw params, effect-instance context, linked spell row/projectile fields when present, call mode, target/beam/attachment data, transform tuple, miss flag, and source profile. Caching only by `progfx` row ID can replay a beam/projectile/node effect in the wrong context.
   - Output should be a typed payload with `canonicalStatus = unsupported | preserveOnly | previewOnly | canonicalCandidate`, resource edges, required context slots, and diagnostics. This keeps future rendering incremental without losing the raw Aurora/EE evidence.

## Aurora Effect Entry And Attachment Contract

`visualeffects.2da` row parsing is not enough. A runtime VFX instance also carries application context.

1. Script/runtime entry is an effect object first.
   - `EffectVisualEffect` constructs a visual-effect effect using a `visualeffects.2da` row ID.
   - The target/application API then decides whether the effect is played at a location, attached to an object, persisted as a duration effect, or sent as an instant visual to nearby clients.
   - `ApplyEffectAtLocation` should be treated as instant/fire-and-forget for normal VFX readiness. Do not persist it as an area-owned duration visual unless the source data is an explicit persistent/AOE path.
   - `ApplyEffectAtLocation` is a generic effect API and may be used with AOE/summon/swarm effects; this report's forced-instant rule is for normal `EffectVisualEffect` VFX preview readiness, not for all non-VFX effect systems.
   - `ApplyEffectToObject` with temporary/permanent duration only stays duration-like for rows whose `Type_FD` supports it.
   - External evidence says rows with `Type_FD = F` or `P` are coerced toward instant behavior, while `D` and `B` support duration behavior.
   - External evidence also says instant object-applied visuals are sent to clients currently in range rather than becoming a durable area object. A browser/editor preview can show them, but export/runtime semantics should not store them as persistent scene children.
   - `ApplyEffectToObject` has target-usability constraints in external API docs; static placeables and non-object/location targets need diagnostics before a VFX instance is treated as object-attached runtime truth.
   - Multiple duration VFX applications using the same row ID can collapse to one visible effect, while row reuse with a different transform may require removal/reapply delay before the changed transform is visible. Treat this as a retail-validation target for cache invalidation and effect refresh, not as a parser fact.
   - `EffectLinkEffects` can carry a visual alongside a non-visual effect, but a link containing only visual effects is documented as unreliable for saved/duration playback. Store link context when available and emit diagnostics instead of assuming a linked VFX is a standalone duration visual.
   - A targeted local decompilation/string search did not expose named `EffectVisualEffect`, `EffectBeam`, `ApplyEffectToObject`, `ApplyEffectAtLocation`, `GetEffectInteger`, `GetEffectFloat`, `GetEffectVector`, `BODY_NODE_*`, or `EFFECT_TYPE_*` symbols in this Ghidra export. Use local `visualeffects` table/emitter evidence as primary for source/model/rendering, and mark constructor/context slot mapping as external NWScript/retail-observation evidence until the runtime function bodies are recovered.
   - Source: https://nwnlexicon.com/index.php/EffectVisualEffect
   - Source: https://nwnlexicon.com/ApplyEffectToObject
   - Source: https://nwnlexicon.com/ApplyEffectAtLocation
   - Source: https://www.nwnlexicon.com/EffectLinkEffects

2. Preserve EE transform data on the effect instance.
   - EE added `fScale`, `vTranslate`, and `vRotate` to `EffectVisualEffect`.
   - EE added the same transform tuple to `EffectBeam`.
   - Store these as effect-instance transforms, not as MDL emitter fields and not as object `SetObjectVisualTransform` state. An object's visual scale/rotation/translation may affect the target/owner presentation layer, but it is a separate script/API lane from the VFX instance tuple carried by `EffectVisualEffect` or `EffectBeam`.
   - Mark them profile-gated: unavailable/unknown in legacy 1.69-style profiles, supported in EE 1.80.8193.14+ evidence.
   - Transform space is described externally as relative to the parented object. Do not bake it into source MDL coordinates at parse time.
   - `EffectVisualEffect` runtime observation evidence maps `GetEffectInteger(0)` to `nVisualEffectId`, `GetEffectInteger(2)` to `nMissEffect`, `GetEffectFloat(0)` to `fScale`, `GetEffectVector(0)` to `vTranslate`, and `GetEffectVector(1)` to `vRotate`.
   - Source: https://www.beamdog.com/news/patch-819315-neverwinter-nights-enhanced-edition/
   - Source: https://nwnlexicon.com/index.php/EffectVisualEffect

2.1. Effect-instance transforms are a layer above selected VFX attachment, not source MDL rewrites.
   - Local MDL parsing already has its own `position`, `orientation`, and `scale` direct/key/bezier-key families on model nodes. Those source-node fields remain raw MDL data and must not be overwritten by EE effect-constructor transform parameters.
   - The effect transform tuple belongs to the applied effect instance and must be stored with constructor/application provenance: constructor kind (`EffectVisualEffect` or `EffectBeam`), application mode (`ApplyEffectToObject` or `ApplyEffectAtLocation`), selected row/phase/root-size slot, target object/location, attachment namespace, miss flag, and EE runtime profile.
   - A renderer-ready transform stack should keep separate layers for target/location anchor, object visual-transform state when the target object has one, row/phase/root attachment selection, EE effect transform tuple, source model node animation transforms, emitter runtime transform cache, and per-particle basis/size/rotation.
   - Exact EE multiplication order, rotation-vector convention, and axis order are not proven by this local decompilation export. Until a retail fixture or recovered branch closes that gap, preview math can display the transform but must emit `VFX_EFFECT_TRANSFORM_ORDER_RETAIL_UNVERIFIED` before claiming parity.
   - `fScale` is not particle `sizeStart/sizeEnd`, chunk model `sizeStart/sizeEnd`, MDL node `scale`, Blender object scale, or Three.js scene scale. It is an effect-instance visual transform with profile provenance.
   - `vTranslate` is not source MDL `position`, emitter `xsize/ysize` spawn rectangle, P2P target offset, or Blender object location. It is an applied-effect offset relative to the parented object/location context described by EE docs.
   - `vRotate` is not MDL `orientationkey`, emitter `render` billboarding, `particleRot`, Blender particle rotation, or row `OrientWithObject`. It is a separate applied-effect rotation transform whose exact retail order must stay diagnostic.
   - Object visual transforms are not object physics/location. External docs explicitly separate visual translation from `GetPosition`/click/pathfinding behavior. If a VFX target has object visual transform state, preserve it as target-presentation context and diagnostics; do not use it to rewrite source row position, phase attachment namespace, AOE footprint, beam endpoint identity, or saved object coordinates.
   - Object visual-transform lerp state is profile/client-state evidence. It may restart for clients that lose perception and `GetObjectVisualTransform(..., bCurrentLerp=TRUE)` is documented with a bug caveat. Treat current-lerp values as observation/profile data until a retail fixture proves selected-client behavior.
   - Effect-instance cache keys must include the transform tuple. External evidence says duplicate same-row duration VFX and changed transforms can require remove/reapply behavior before the visual changes, so a browser/runtime cache must not reuse one stale row-only instance for different transforms.
   - If object visual transforms are included in preview, cache keys need a separate object visual-transform hash plus scope/lerp state; do not fold it into the effect tuple.

3. `nMissEffect` is effect-instance state.
   - Preserve the flag.
   - External behavior says it selects a random nearby/past-target location and is most applicable to instant visuals, beams, or projectiles.
   - Do not implement it as a stable emitter offset or as a reusable model transform.
   - Do not implement it as emitter randomness. It is not `randvel`, `spread`, `velocity`, spawn rectangle noise, Blender particle randomization, PoC random offsets, or frontend sprite drift.
   - Record raw and normalized flag values with constructor/application provenance. The provenance tuple should include effect kind, row ID, source profile, application mode, target/location before miss policy, selected post-policy event location when observable, and the scheduler/cache status that used the flag.
   - Duration-row + miss-effect combinations should be diagnostic because external evidence describes them as visually unreliable/instant-like.
   - A miss effect that becomes instant must use event-style preview/cache handling, not the duration effect cache key.
   - Required diagnostics: `VFX_EFFECT_MISS_FLAG_EFFECT_INSTANCE_FIELD` when the flag is present in constructor state, `VFX_EFFECT_MISS_NOT_EMITTER_RANDOMNESS` when an adapter tries to map it to emitter/preview randomness, and `VFX_EFFECT_MISS_DURATION_POLICY_UNVERIFIED` for duration rows until a retail fixture or recovered Aurora branch proves stable selected-profile behavior.
   - Source: https://nwnlexicon.com/index.php/EffectVisualEffect

4. Beam effect instances need source, target, and body-node context.
   - `EffectBeam` carries `nBeamVisualEffect`, `oEffector`, `nBodyPart`, `bMissEffect`, and EE transform data.
   - The applied object/location is the beam target context; `oEffector` is the source object.
   - `nBodyPart` selects the source attachment node/body node.
   - Do not confuse `oEffector` with the effect creator. External NWScript evidence says the effect creator is the object/script context that constructed the effect, while `EffectBeam`'s `oEffector` is the runtime beam source object. These can diverge when effects are constructed on one object and applied/assigned through another.
   - Implementation consequence: store `effectCreatorRef` only as observation/provenance when available; store `beamSourceObjectRef` from `oEffector` as the canonical beam source input. A missing source object must not fall back silently to creator, target, or applying object.
   - Effect creator provenance still matters for linked duration effects, removal diagnostics, and retail fixture interpretation. Do not drop creator data just because it is not a beam source.
   - External `BODY_NODE_*` names are `HAND`, `CHEST`, and `MONSTER_0..9`, but the exact model-node lookup/fallback policy must still be validated against runtime behavior.
   - NWN Lexicon's `BODY_NODE_*` table explicitly says monster nodes are not present on every model by default. Missing source nodes must therefore produce beam-body-node diagnostics, not synthetic fallback endpoints.
   - `BODY_NODE_*` is not the same namespace as creature appearance body parts. Local `BodyPart_LFoot`/`BodyPart_RHand`/`BodyPart_LHand` strings are read/written in creature appearance/body-part GFF code and correspond to part-based creature model data, not beam source anchors.
   - Keep beam body-node references as an `AuroraBeamBodyNodeRef` style field, separate from any future `AuroraCreatureBodyPartRef`/`CREATURE_PART_*` appearance handling.
   - `EffectVisualEffect` can reference beam rows, but external evidence warns that `EffectBeam` is the proper constructor for beam source-node context.
   - The same external evidence says generic `EffectVisualEffect` appears to use an implicit effector/source-node policy for beam-like rows. Preserve this as `implicitBeamContextUnverified` or equivalent when a `Type_FD = B` row arrives through generic `EffectVisualEffect`; do not silently upgrade it to `EffectBeam`, and do not substitute creator/target/applying object until retail or decompilation evidence proves the default.
   - Preserve unresolved source object and body-node data. Do not synthesize a beam from emitter render mode.
   - Local Aurora string evidence has `PartBeam`, `m_bOrientWithTarget`, and beam-volume shader vocabulary, supporting a separate beam-family/runtime lane, but this export did not expose direct `EffectBeam` function names or a visible `m_bOrientWithTarget` C call site.
   - The local `BodyPart_*` decompilation call sites below are creature appearance read/write evidence only. Keep them under the namespace-separation proof; do not use them as beam body-node proof.

4.1. Explicit beam admission requires an `AuroraVfxBeamContext` record.
   - Canonical browser beam rendering must not start from a bare `visualeffects.2da` row, a `Type_FD = B` value, a `VFX_BEAM_*` constant, local `PartBeam` vocabulary, mesh `beaming`, spell/toolset `fxbeam`, or beam-volume shader strings.
   - First create a preserve-first `AuroraVfxBeamContext`/`AuroraBeamEffectContext` record. Minimum fields: constructed effect kind (`EffectBeam`), `visualeffects.2da` physical row ID and raw source token, selected source/profile, explicit `oEffector`/beam source object, applied target object or location, raw `nBodyPart`, normalized external `BODY_NODE_*` label when known, `bMissEffect`, duration/application mode, effect creator provenance as a separate non-source field, EE transform tuple plus profile gate, and diagnostics.
   - Add observation-only fields for `GetEffectInteger`/`GetEffectFloat`/`GetEffectVector`/`GetEffectObject` captures when a retail EE fixture provides them. These slots help validate implementation behavior, but they do not replace constructor/application inputs.
   - `GetEffectObject` beam object-index mapping remains observation-only until a scripted retail fixture or recovered function body proves which index corresponds to effector/source/target. Do not use an unproven accessor index as canonical source context.
   - Preserve source-row beam evidence (`Type_FD = B`, `VFX_BEAM_*`, `progfx.2da` Type 7) inside the context as row-family/progfx evidence only. It proves which visual family was requested, not that endpoints, source object, or source body node are known.
   - Generic `EffectVisualEffect` on a beam row may enter a separate `implicitBeamContextUnverified`/preview-only bucket, but it must not share cache identity with explicit `EffectBeam` and must not be silently upgraded to `effectKind = beam`.
   - Cache keys for explicit beams must include row ID/source profile, constructed effect kind, source object, target object/location, body-node value, miss flag, duration/application mode, EE transform tuple/profile, and the explicit-vs-implicit beam policy. Missing any of those context dimensions emits diagnostics instead of reusing a row-only preview.
   - Local `PartBeam`, `m_bOrientWithTarget`, `vs_beamvol`/`fs_beamvol`, `beaming`, and `fxbeam` evidence should be attached as lane/provenance evidence only. None of them is enough to synthesize endpoints or body-node anchors without effect-instance context.

7.5. Attachment anchor resolution is target-class and namespace specific.
   - A `visualeffects.2da` row chooses phase resources; it does not by itself prove the final target node. The runtime effect instance still needs target class, application mode, phase, and source/target object context before attachment can be canonical.
   - NWN Wiki's model-special-node page gives placeable and door dummy-node naming rules: crop the first four characters of the model name and append a suffix such as `_impact`, `_head`, `_hand`, or `_ground` for placeables, and `_impc`, `_head`, `_head_hit`, or `_grnd` for doors.
   - That same source says these placeable/door nodes are optional and missing nodes fall back to the center/location of the object. Preserve this as an explicit fallback provenance, not as proof that every VFX family can silently center-fallback.
   - The source's creature section is marked TODO, so it is not enough to define creature VFX special-node lookup. Creature-targeted head/hand/impact behavior needs retail capture or deeper runtime recovery before canonical browser parity can be claimed.
   - Local Aurora string evidence contains `impact`, `rhand`, `lhand`, and spell/toolset slots such as `fxhead`/`fximpact`, but this is vocabulary/source-slot evidence, not a complete attachment resolver.
   - Beam `BODY_NODE_*` constants are effect-instance source anchors, not placeable/door special dummies and not creature appearance `BodyPart_*` GFF fields.
   - Implementation consequence: future code needs an `AuroraVfxAttachmentRequest` carrying `targetClass`, `targetModelResRef`, `phase`, `attachmentNamespace`, requested node/body-node value, fallback policy, source row/column, and diagnostics. A single untyped `nodeName` is not enough.

7.5.1. Attachment resolver input/output contract.
   - Input must include `targetClass` (`creature`, `placeable`, `door`, `areaObject`, `item`, `location`, or `unknown`), `targetObjectRef` when present, `targetModelResRef`, selected `visualeffects.2da` row ID/source profile, selected phase, selected phase slot, attachment namespace, target size/root category when relevant, and row flags such as `BodyNode`, `OrientWithGround`, `OrientWithObject`, and `InheritScale`.
   - Attachment namespaces must be explicit. Minimum namespaces are `phaseHeadCon`, `phaseImpact`, `phaseRootSize`, `visualeffectsBodyNode`, `beamBodyNode`, `progfxModelNode`, `placeableDoorSpecialNode`, `creatureSpecialNodeUnverified`, `aoeFootprint`, and `spellToolsetSourceSlot`.
   - Output must be a resolved-anchor record, not a raw string: `resolvedAnchorKind = modelNode | centerFallback | locationOnly | unresolved`, plus `nodeName`, `fallbackKind`, `fallbackEvidence`, `targetModelVersion`, `sourceFieldPath`, and diagnostics.
   - A selected empty phase slot, a missing phase model resource, and a missing target attachment node are three different failures. Do not report all of them as "missing model".
   - Placeable/door center fallback is allowed only when the resolver is using the external placeable/door special-node convention and records that specific source. Do not apply that fallback to beam `BODY_NODE_*`, creature special nodes, ProgFX Type 12 target nodes, phase model resource misses, or sound-only rows.
   - Creature-targeted phase anchors remain runtime-unverified in this export. Local `BodyPart_*` GFF fields and local `rhand`/`lhand` strings are not enough to select a creature head/hand/root node without a recovered runtime resolver or retail fixture.
   - Orientation flags are applied to the phase/spawned-model transform policy after anchor selection. They do not change MDL emitter `render`, particle billboard basis, atlas UVs, Blender particle orientation, or beam source/body-node selection unless a recovered branch proves that behavior.
   - A location-applied normal `EffectVisualEffect` has no target model namespace. It can preview a phase model at a location, but must emit location-only attachment diagnostics instead of resolving `HeadCon`, `Root_*`, `BodyNode`, or placeable/door special nodes.
   - Implementation consequence: cache keys for attached VFX must include attachment namespace and resolved-anchor provenance, not just row ID and target object ID.
   - Sources: https://nwn.wiki/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=38176277, https://nwnlexicon.com/Body_node, https://www.gamebanshee.com/news/74027-neverwinter-nights-v1.64-now-available.html

7.6. Phase scheduling is an effect-instance matrix, not a source-row default.
   - A parsed `visualeffects.2da` row should produce source facts; it should not immediately schedule impact, duration, or cessation playback.
   - `ApplyEffectAtLocation` is documented as the normal location path for visual effects, but external behavior notes say normal visual-effect duration is not durably stored there. Treat location-applied normal VFX as event-style playback unless the constructed effect is an explicit AOE/summon/swarm/persistent path.
   - `ApplyEffectToObject` with `DURATION_TYPE_INSTANT` should create an event-style object visual visible to currently relevant clients, not a persisted scene child or a long-lived editor object.
   - `ApplyEffectToObject` with temporary/permanent duration can schedule durable VFX only when the constructed effect, row `Type_FD`, miss flag, and target object support it. External behavior says `Type_FD = F` and `P` tend toward instant handling, while `D` and `B` can persist.
   - A miss visual is effect-instance state and is externally described as instant/unreliable for duration rows. It must force a diagnostic/cache split instead of being modeled as a stable emitter transform.
   - Duration rows need separate phase events: impact at application, duration while active, and cessation at removal. `SoundImpact`, `SoundDuration`, `SoundCessastion`, `ProgFX_Impact`, `ProgFX_Duration`, `ProgFX_Cessation`, and impact/cessation model slots must therefore remain separate inputs to an `AuroraVfxPhaseSchedule`.
   - External notes say repeated duration VFX applications by the same row ID can collapse visually, and transform changes may require removal plus a small reapply delay before becoming visible. Treat this as cache/retail-validation evidence, not a parser-side dedup rule.
   - Do not confuse that remove/reapply delay observation with cross-profile `DelayDurationFX`. The former is an effect-instance cache/retail-fixture concern; the latter is an NWN2/custom source column unless the selected profile proves otherwise, and using it as the reapply-delay source should emit `VFX_2DA_DELAY_DURATION_FX_NOT_REAPPLY_DELAY`.
   - `ApplyEffectToObject` requires a usable/non-static target for object-attached effects according to external API docs. Missing/invalid target object context must block canonical duration scheduling even when the row data parses cleanly.
   - Implementation consequence: domain state needs `AuroraVfxPhaseSchedule` with `constructedEffectKind`, `applicationMode`, `durationType`, `requestedDuration`, `rowTypeFd`, `missFlag`, `targetKind`, `targetObjectUsability`, `phase`, `phaseSourceRefs`, and diagnostics. A renderer that receives only a row ID or MDL resref must stay preview-only.
   - Local decompilation in this export proves the `visualeffects` source-table bootstrap and emitter runtime paths, but not these NWScript scheduling rules. Keep the scheduling matrix under external/profile provenance until retail fixtures or a recovered client branch prove it.
   - Source: https://nwnlexicon.com/index.php/EffectVisualEffect
   - Source: https://nwnlexicon.com/ApplyEffectAtLocation
   - Source: https://nwnlexicon.com/ApplyEffectToObject
   - Source for phase columns: https://gitea.raptio.us/tinygiant/PRC8/src/commit/f491984d6b5399483ab491ece74204d16154819e/NWN%20.35-33%202DAs/visualeffects.2da

7.7. AOE/persistent VFX is a separate effect/object lane.
   - `EffectAreaOfEffect` constructs an area-of-effect effect from `vfx_persistent.2da`. It is not `EffectVisualEffect`, not `EffectBeam`, and not a `ProgFX_Duration` phase.
   - The AOE row ID belongs to the `vfx_persistent.2da` namespace. Do not cache or resolve it as a `visualeffects.2da` row, even if the row later references `DurationVFX` or model/spawn visual fields.
   - AOE application creates a pseudo-object / `OBJECT_TYPE_AREA_OF_EFFECT` style runtime object with a tag from the row `LABEL`, creator/spell metadata when available, location or followed-object context, and event scripts.
   - AOE scripts (`ONENTER`, `HEARTBEAT`, `ONEXIT`, plus externally documented user-defined event support) are script resrefs. They must not be interpreted as MDL emitter names, Blender Geometry Nodes callbacks, Three.js events, or visual resource refs.
   - Mobile AOE and static AOE differ: mobile rows follow an applied object and can be dispelled/removed with the parent effect; static rows exist at a location and must be found/destroyed as AOE objects. Keep this split in the domain model.
   - Shape and footprint are table/profile data: circle/rectangle, radius/width/length, and optional spawned visual models/sounds must stay tied to the AOE row and application context.
   - External 2DA evidence marks `vfx_persistent.2da` as client/server loaded, not toolset-loaded, and records profile-dependent row limits: modern EE documentation says `2147483647` in patch `8193.36`, while older/mobile-object usage had a `0..255` limit. Store this as selected-profile evidence instead of reusing the `visualeffects.2da` `uint16` row-ID rule.
   - External 2DA evidence also marks `areaeffects.2da` as unused and points to `vfx_persistent.2da` instead. A future resolver should preserve an encountered `areaeffects.2da` file as unsupported/cross-profile evidence, not silently alias it into canonical AOE runtime rows.
   - Lexicon `EFFECT_TYPE` evidence records `EFFECT_TYPE_AREA_OF_EFFECT = 20` and notes that these effects tend to create objects. Treat this as external effect-type evidence that reinforces the pseudo-object lane, not as local Aurora body proof.
   - The local decompilation export did not expose `vfx_persistent` or `EffectAreaOfEffect`. Therefore this AOE lane is required by external NWScript/NWN1 docs, but exact runtime cadence, object-update timing, shape inclusion tests, creator propagation, and model-spawn randomness remain retail/decompilation validation targets.
   - Diagnostics: `VFX_AOE_ROW_LIMIT_PROFILE_REQUIRED`, `VFX_AOE_ROW_LIMIT_NOT_VISUALEFFECTS_WORD`, `VFX_AOE_AREAEFFECTS_UNUSED_TABLE`, and `VFX_AOE_EFFECT_TYPE_OBJECT_CREATION_EXTERNAL`.
   - Implementation consequence: future code needs `AuroraAreaOfEffectSourceRow`, `AuroraAoeEffectInstance`, and `AuroraAoeRuntimeObject` concepts. A normal `AuroraVfxPhaseSchedule` for `visualeffects.2da` must not synthesize them.
   - Source: https://nwnlexicon.com/EffectAreaOfEffect
   - Source: https://nwn.wiki/spaces/NWN1/pages/38175203/vfx_persistent.2da
   - Source for row limits and unused `areaeffects.2da`: https://nwn.wiki/spaces/NWN1/pages/38174875/2da%2BFiles
   - Source for effect type: https://nwnlexicon.com/EFFECT_TYPE

7.7.1. AOE runtime objects need admission gates.
   - Create `AuroraAoeRuntimeObject` only from an `AuroraAreaOfEffectSourceRow` plus an `AuroraAoeEffectInstance`. A row-only import can preserve data, and an effect-instance-only script trace can preserve intent, but neither one is enough to create a canonical persistent AOE object.
   - Minimum `AuroraAoeRuntimeObject` fields: source table `vfx_persistent.2da`, physical row ID, row `LABEL`/tag, source profile/layer/hash, constructed effect kind `EffectAreaOfEffect`, static/mobile application mode, duration type/requested duration, creator/effect-creator provenance, spell ID/caster-level metadata when observable, anchor location or followed-object reference, event script refs with resource class `script`, shape footprint, visual footprint refs, sound footprint refs, lifecycle state, resolver edges, and diagnostics.
   - Shape footprint is not optional for canonical preview: circle rows need radius, rectangle rows need width/length plus orientation context. Missing or profile-only shape evidence can still render a marked preview overlay, but must not enter canonical runtime payloads.
   - `DurationVFX`, `VisualFX`, `MODEL01..MODEL03`, model counts/durations/edge weights, and low-quality alternates are AOE visual-footprint refs. They may later produce nested model/VFX dependency edges inside an AOE runtime object, but they do not create normal `AuroraVfxPhaseSchedule` records unless an explicit AOE-footprint interpreter has already preserved the AOE owner context.
   - AOE sound fields are sound-footprint refs on the AOE object. Impact/duration/cessation timing, looping, replay to clients entering range, and voice ownership remain profile/retail validation targets until local runtime evidence is recovered.
   - AOE cache keys are separate from normal VFX keys and must include source table, row ID, source profile/hash, static/mobile mode, anchor location or followed object, creator/effect creator, spell metadata when known, requested duration, shape footprint, event script refs, visual/sound footprint refs, and selected runtime profile. The same AOE row at another location, with another creator, or following a different object is a different runtime object.
   - Lifecycle state is part of the contract. At minimum preserve `created`, `active`, `removed`, `expired`, `dispelled`, and `destroyed/invalid-anchor` style states as observed or inferred states, with unknown ordering recorded instead of guessed.
   - Browser/Blender/Three preview admission: source row plus effect instance plus shape footprint may show a footprint overlay or annotated preview object. A normal `ApplyEffectAtLocation(EffectVisualEffect(...))`, a raw model ref, or a persistent scene child from the POC cannot synthesize an AOE runtime object.
   - Local Aurora proof remains negative for the specific table/function names: `ONHEARTBEAT` string hits prove only generic event vocabulary, not `vfx_persistent.2da` schema, heartbeat cadence, or AOE object construction.

9. Item-property visual effects are a separate entry family.
   - `ItemPropertyVisualEffect` constructs an item-property visual for melee weapon glow and is described externally as purely visual item-property data.
   - Aurora's local `iprp_visualfx` load plus `ModelSuffix` lookup supports keeping this path separate from script-applied `EffectVisualEffect`.
   - Lexicon `ITEM_VISUAL_*` constants line up with the local Aurora fallback switch: acid `0`, cold `1`, electrical `2`, fire `3`, sonic `4`, holy `5`, and evil `6`; the local fallback suffix for value `6` is `_fxneg`, so keep both the external constant label and the local suffix literal as provenance rather than renaming one into the other.
   - Local Aurora fallback suffixes for missing `ModelSuffix` are item-property fallback evidence only. Preserve whether the suffix came from the source table or from hardcoded fallback.
   - NWN:EE notes add custom weapon visual effects through `iprp_visualfx.2da`. That strengthens the table-source path, but in this Aurora-first report it stays separate from classic/local hardcoded fallback and from normal `visualeffects.2da` row parsing.
   - Do not route `ItemPropertyVisualEffect` through `Type_FD`, impact/duration/cessation phases, or beam body nodes.
   - A canonical preview request needs item-property application context: owning item object/resref, equipped slot or visible weapon model context, subtype, selected `iprp_visualfx.2da` row/profile, resolved suffix source (`table` or `auroraFallback`), and diagnostics. Without that, keep the suffix as source data only.
   - External evidence says this is melee-weapon-only; non-melee, unequipped, missing item, or missing visible weapon-model context must emit item-property diagnostics instead of spawning a loose emitter or phase model.
   - NWN Wiki lists `iprp_visualfx.2da` as extendable in EE but still constrained to `0..255` because the subtype is `uint8_t`; this matches the local decompilation reading the subtype from a byte-like field before lookup. Store the width/profile evidence with the source row and do not reuse `visualeffects.2da` row-width rules.
   - `ModelSuffix` should be treated as a model suffix/variant-resolution input. Do not turn it into a phase MDL resref, a texture name, a `ProgFX` row, a beam row, or a Blender material preset. Exact suffix-to-resource composition remains retail/recovered-branch work.
   - `ModelSuffix` and hardcoded `_fx*` suffix literals are also not source-list/palette VFX entries. PoC/frontend kind heuristics such as `label starts with VFX:` or `resref starts with fx_` can classify placed objects for UI browsing, but must not classify item-property suffix strings as `placedVfxPlaceable`, `visualeffectsRow`, source-list resrefs, or standalone MDL/model resources.

## Blender And NeverBlender Interpretation

Blender/NeverBlender is useful for authoring and round-trip evidence, but not as Aurora runtime truth.

### Blender operational model for Aurora VFX work

Blender has to be treated as several different surfaces, not one VFX truth source:

1. Authoring data-blocks:
   - `ParticleSettings` is a reusable Blender ID data-block. It owns Blender-side settings such as `count`, `frame_start`, `frame_end`, `lifetime`, `physics_type`, `render_type`, `normal_factor`, `factor_random`, `angular_velocity_factor`, object/collection instancing targets, display settings, and animation/custom-property support inherited from Blender RNA/ID.
   - Because it is reusable, `ParticleSettings` identity is not enough to identify an Aurora emitter. The importer needs a tuple such as Blender object ID/name, particle-system modifier/index/name, particle-settings ID/name, and NeverBlender node provenance before it can attach the settings to one normalized emitter source.
   - This makes it a convenient add-on metadata carrier, which is exactly what NeverBlender uses.
   - Blender's current `bpy.props` API supports attaching registered `PropertyGroup` data to Blender data types via `PointerProperty`; NeverBlender uses this exact pattern for `bpy.types.ParticleSettings.nvb`.
   - The custom-property schema is add-on-defined. If a `.blend` is opened or inspected without the NeverBlender property classes registered, the importer must report schema/provenance uncertainty instead of treating missing `settings.nvb` data as proof that Aurora fields were absent.
   - Blender animation data and F-Curves target RNA data paths. NeverBlender's emitter actions therefore keyframe Blender paths such as `nvb.birthrate` or `normal_factor`, but those paths are still Blender authoring paths, not Aurora runtime offsets.
   - Current Blender Action docs describe `Action.fcurves` as a legacy/backward-compatible view of the first action slot in the layered-action model. NeverBlender's `action.fcurves` usage therefore needs Blender-version and action-slot provenance if future tooling reads or writes `.blend` actions directly.
   - If a Blender Action contains layered/slotted animation beyond the legacy first slot, a future importer must preserve the extra action/slot metadata as `blenderAuthoring` and emit an unresolved-slot diagnostic until an Aurora mapping is proven.
   - Blender F-Curves can evaluate at arbitrary frames and can contain keyframes, sampled points, modifiers, mute/valid state, and extrapolation. NeverBlender exports evaluated values only at keyed frames for known data paths, so Blender curve handles/modifiers/sampled data are authoring-only unless raw Aurora key data is preserved separately.
   - Implementation consequence: if we ingest Blender/NeverBlender data, read `ParticleSettings.nvb` and the few native storage fields as an authoring carrier only, then normalize them back to Aurora field names.
   - Official API source: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.ParticleSettings.html
   - Property API source: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.props.html
   - Animation data API source: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.AnimData.html
   - Action API source: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.Action.html
   - F-Curve API source: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.FCurve.html

2. Evaluated simulation state:
   - `ParticleSystem` is the evaluated object-level particle system. It owns generated `particles`, `child_particles`, `point_cache`, `settings`, random seeds, target particle systems, editability flags, and current simulation-step state.
   - `Particle` state exposes values such as birth/death/lifetime, current and previous position/velocity/rotation, size, and alive state, but those values belong to Blender's solver.
   - Implementation consequence: do not import Blender evaluated particles, child particles, path cache, point cache, baked state, or `ParticleData.prev_location` as Aurora runtime particles. Aurora has its own active/free list, reset path, previous-position slots, atlas UV generation, and six-vertex draw buffer.
   - Official API source: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.ParticleSystem.html
   - Particle API source: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.Particle.html

3. Render-as and viewport output:
   - Blender emitter render modes are `None`, `Halo`, `Path`, `Object`, and `Collection`; the manual describes object/collection modes as instancing render outputs.
   - Current Blender 4.5 LTS manual frames the Render panel as controlling how Blender particles appear when rendered. `None` suppresses particle rendering, `Halo` is a Blender halo/dot style, `Path` is tied to hair/keyed path visualization, and `Object`/`Collection` instance Blender objects/collections at particle positions.
   - The same manual notes that Cycles supports only `Object` and `Collection` render types. This is Blender renderer capability, not evidence that Aurora chunk particles should be implemented as Blender object/collection instances.
   - Official API also exposes `render_type` values such as `NONE`, `HALO`, `LINE`, `PATH`, `OBJECT`, and `COLLECTION`.
   - Cycles support is narrower for particle render types, which reinforces that these are Blender renderer choices, not portable Aurora VFX semantics.
   - Implementation consequence: never map Blender `render_type` to Aurora emitter `render`. In particular, Blender `Object`/`Collection` instancing is not Aurora `chunkName`; Aurora chunk particles resolve MDL resources and use Aurora lifetime/resource cleanup.
   - Manual source: https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/physics/particles/emitter/render.html

4. Emission timing and cache:
   - Blender emitter particles are emitted from a selected object from a frame start to frame end, have a maximum parent-particle count, use a seed, and are frame/cache driven.
   - Current Blender 4.5 LTS cache docs say the emitter particle system uses Blender's unified cache/bake system, calculates the simulation only for positive frames inside the Cache panel start/end range, writes frames into cache during playback, and protects baked simulations from automatic recalculation until the bake is cleared.
   - Particle Edit constraints are also cache-state dependent: Blender can require a memory bake and disallow editing with disk cache. This is an authoring/editability rule, not an Aurora emitter validity rule.
   - Geometry Nodes simulation zones are also frame-state/cached systems; baking stores intermediate geometry and Blender explicitly does not treat baked geometry data as a general import/export format.
   - Implementation consequence: Blender frame ranges, seeds, cache validity, and Geometry Nodes baked state can drive a Blender preview, but not the canonical browser runtime. Aurora runtime timing comes from Aurora fields and effect application lifetime.
   - Manual source: https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/physics/particles/emitter/emission.html
   - Cache source: https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/physics/particles/emitter/cache.html
   - Simulation source: https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/4.0/modeling/geometry_nodes/simulation/simulation_zone.html
   - Baking source: https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/baking.html

5. Material/alpha preview:
   - Blender material alpha has API/version drift: older/current compatibility surfaces expose `blend_method` (`OPAQUE`, `CLIP`, `HASHED`, `BLEND`), while newer Blender API notes point toward `surface_render_method` (`DITHERED`, `BLENDED`).
   - Older Eevee material settings distinguish `Opaque`, `Alpha Clip`, `Alpha Hashed`, and `Alpha Blending`; current Blender 4.5 LTS documentation presents the newer render-method surface (`Dithered`/`Blended`) for EEVEE material transparency.
   - Blender documentation warns that transparent sorting is object-level, not per-fragment/per-triangle, so Blender transparency order is only an authoring/preview caveat.
   - Implementation consequence: use Blender alpha settings only as preview hints. They do not define Aurora `Normal`, `Punch-Through`, fallback/Lighten-candidate, `renderorder`, depth-write, state-`0` transparency, or engine state-`1` punch-through behavior.
   - API source: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.Material.html
   - Manual source: https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/4.0/render/eevee/materials/settings.html
   - Current material-settings source: https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/render/eevee/material_settings.html

6. Version-captured Blender authoring metadata:
   - As of the current Blender API/manual check, Blender still exposes `Material.blend_method`, but marks it deprecated in favor of `surface_render_method`.
   - Blender 4.2 Eevee migration notes describe the material render-method transition, including `Dithered` and `Blended` behavior; current 4.5 LTS material docs continue that render-method framing.
   - Implementation consequence: a `.blend`-origin VFX import must record Blender version, render engine, source alpha property (`blend_method` or `surface_render_method`), and authoring FPS. These are preview/export-diff facts only; they cannot change Aurora emitter `blend`.
   - API source: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.Material.html
   - Release-note source: https://developer.blender.org/docs/release_notes/4.2/python_api/
   - Eevee migration source: https://developer.blender.org/docs/release_notes/4.2/eevee_migration/
   - Current material-settings source: https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/render/eevee/material_settings.html

7. Blender has no single Aurora-equivalent VFX runtime surface.
   - Legacy/object particles, material transparency, object/collection particle instancing, point caches, hair/path visualization, and Geometry Nodes simulations are different Blender systems with different ownership and cache rules.
   - `ParticleSettings` is authoring/settings data, `ParticleSystem` is evaluated object state, `Particle` is solver output, and `PointCache` is physics cache state.
   - Geometry Nodes simulation zones are node-graph state machines evaluated across frames and cached/baked by Blender; they can be powerful preview tooling, but they are not MDL `node emitter` rows, 2DA visual-effect references, or Aurora active/free particle lists.
   - Implementation consequence: future Blender integration must expose a `BlenderVfxAuthoringEnvelope`, not a `BlenderVfxRuntime`. That envelope can carry Blender version, object names, particle-settings IDs, F-Curves, point-cache status, material preview flags, and Geometry Nodes preview graph IDs, while canonical runtime state still comes from `auroraRaw`/`auroraNormalized`.
   - Official API/manual sources: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.ParticleSettings.html, https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.ParticleSystem.html, https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.PointCache.html, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/4.0/modeling/geometry_nodes/simulation/simulation_zone.html

8. Blender previous/current particle data is name-compatible but not provenance-compatible.
   - Blender exposes current and previous particle values through evaluated particle data, but these values belong to Blender's solver and cache lifecycle.
   - Aurora `Motion_Blur` previous-position slots are runtime state updated by Aurora emitter update families and consumed by the Aurora vertex builder.
   - Implementation consequence: a Blender import can record that a preview particle has previous/current state, but it must never use Blender previous locations to satisfy `VFX_RENDER_MOTION_BLUR_ENDPOINT_PREVIOUS_POSITION_REQUIRED`.
   - Official API source: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.Particle.html

9. Blender material alpha describes viewport/render behavior, not Aurora draw lanes.
   - Blender/Eevee distinguishes alpha clip/hash/blend style behavior and warns that transparent blending depends on draw order with object-level sorting.
   - Aurora textured particles have their own `blend` token mapping, depth-write/cutout branches, render-order field, shader-lane vocabulary, and six-vertex particle buffer.
   - Implementation consequence: a Blender preview material can be generated after Aurora state is parsed, but it must carry `VFX_BLENDER_ALPHA_MODE_PREVIEW_ONLY` and must not decide Aurora `Normal`, `Punch-Through`, fallback/Lighten-candidate, or `particleSoftness`.
   - Official manual source: https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/4.0/render/eevee/materials/settings.html

1. Blender native particles:
   - Emit from an object over Blender frame start/end.
   - Use Blender settings such as count, lifetime, emission source/distribution, random seed, physics type, and render-as mode.
   - Render as Blender particle outputs such as none/path/object/collection according to Blender's renderer, not Aurora's particle shader path.
   - Blender `ParticleSettings.render_type` values are renderer outputs; they do not represent Aurora `Normal`, `Linked`, `Motion_Blur`, `Aligned`, `Billboard_to_Local_Z`, `Billboard_to_World_Z`, chunk-particle behavior, or the separate VFX beam family.
   - Do not map these directly to Aurora `update`, `render`, `blend`, `spawntype`, P2P, `detonate`, `Type_FD`, or `progfx.2da`.
   - Blender F-curves can represent animation on stored settings, but Aurora `fieldkey` and especially `fieldbezierkey` still need an Aurora-specific parser/preserve layer.
   - Blender simulation is cache/bake/frame-range sensitive; Aurora VFX needs deterministic runtime state based on active/free particles, emitter update family, and effect lifetime.
   - Blender source separates reusable `ParticleSettings`, evaluated `ParticleSystem`, `ParticleData`, and `PointCache` state. A correct Aurora renderer must not consume Blender point-cache state, current-frame evaluated particles, child/path caches, or render-as instance settings as canonical Aurora state.
   - Blender `ParticleData` has current and previous particle states, but those are Blender solver states, not Aurora's previous-position slots used by `Motion_Blur`.
   - Blender object/collection instancing is a renderer feature for particles. It is not Aurora `chunkName`, because Aurora chunk particles resolve an MDL resource and follow Aurora chunk-particle lifetime/resource cleanup.
   - Blender `ParticleSettings.physics_type` values such as Newton, Keyed, Boids, and Fluid are solver selections, not Aurora emitter `update` families.
   - Blender frame-start/frame-end/count/lifetime form a Blender emission envelope, not Aurora `birthrate`, `lifeExp`, `spawntype`, `loop`, `detonate`, duration type, or effect-instance lifetime.
   - Do not convert an Aurora Explosion into a Blender count spike, start/end range, or cached burst. Preserve the Aurora event row, evaluate the detonate latch in the Aurora runtime, and use Blender only as authoring/preview metadata.
   - Blender Newtonian/Keyed/Boids/Fluid particle physics are authoring/preview concepts. They must not be used to infer Aurora `mass`, `drag`, `grav`, P2P, `threshold`, collision, or Lightning math.
   - Blender particle rotation/orientation settings are initial/dynamic particle settings; they must not be collapsed into Aurora render-mode billboarding, `Linked`, or `Motion_Blur`.
   - Blender Geometry Nodes simulation can be useful for a future visual preview graph, but it is a separate node-graph simulation model. It must be opt-in preview metadata, not an implicit Aurora VFX implementation.

2. Blender material alpha/blend modes:
   - Can be used to preview transparency behavior, but only as Blender renderer behavior.
   - `Alpha Clip` can illustrate cutout/punch behavior in a Blender preview, but it is not proven to equal Aurora `Punch-Through` and must not be used as fixed-function alpha-test evidence.
   - `Alpha Blending`/transparent sorting limitations in Eevee are especially dangerous for particle-heavy effects; Aurora's own particle order and `renderorder` must be modeled separately.
   - `blend_method` vs `surface_render_method` API drift must be handled as Blender-version compatibility only.
   - Do not let Blender material alpha rewrite emitter `blend`, TXI alpha directives, MTR `transparency`, or particle shader lane selection.

3. NeverBlender source confirms a preserve/export model:
   - Registers Aurora emitter data on `bpy.types.ParticleSettings.nvb`.
   - Parses Aurora emitter fields into custom properties.
   - Creates a Blender particle system but sets `count = 0`.
   - This is the clearest local evidence that imported Aurora emitters are represented as editable metadata, not as Blender-native particle simulations.
   - Storage is split: `velocity`, `randvel`, and `particleRot` are mapped to native Blender `ParticleSettings` fields (`normal_factor`, `factor_random`, `angular_velocity_factor`), while most Aurora-only fields live under `settings.nvb`.
   - Imported emitter `xsize`/`ysize` build an authoring mesh plane in Blender units after cm-to-meter conversion; that plane is not Aurora's particle runtime.
   - Do not trust Blender `ParticleSettings.nvb.particletype` as source truth after import. NeverBlender's import code appears to compare `particletype == 'chunk'/'texture'` instead of assigning it, so `chunkName`/`texture` raw fields must drive our source model.
   - Exports ASCII MDL emitter fields from custom properties.
   - Corrects case-sensitive Aurora tokens such as `Fountain`, `Single`, `Explosion`, `Lightning`, and render/blend strings.
   - Exports normal F-curve animation as `fieldkey`; broad `fieldbezierkey` support was not found.
   - Imports Aurora animation time in seconds into Blender frames through scene FPS, then creates Blender F-Curves with linear interpolation. Export walks keyed Blender frames and writes `fieldkey`, so Blender can be a lossy authoring bridge for timing/interpolation unless raw Aurora tracks are preserved.
   - Reads emitter settings from the active/pinned Blender particle settings context and disables panels when the Blender particle system is baked/edited/non-editable. This is Blender UI state only; it is not an Aurora runtime validity condition.
   - Local source confirms the authoring split: `create_particle_system` writes imported Aurora values into `part_sys_settings.nvb` or selected native Blender fields, then sets `part_sys_settings.count = 0`.
   - Local source confirms export reads `obj.particle_systems.active.settings`, writes Aurora names such as `update`, `render`, `blend`, `birthrate`, `lifeexp`, `velocity`, `randvel`, `particlerot`, `texture`, `chunkName`, P2P, blast, lightning, and inheritance fields.
   - Local source confirms `loop` is a NeverBlender/Aurora authoring field only for `update == single`: the property description says it emits multiple particles when update is `Single`, and the exporter writes `loop` only in the `part_set.nvb.update == 'single'` branch.
   - Local source confirms `lifeexp` is exported as the Aurora MDL `lifeexp` property; it must normalize back to Aurora `lifeExp`/target offset `0x90`, not Blender `ParticleSettings.lifetime`.
   - Local source confirms NeverBlender's emitter property group descriptions are UI/authoring annotations: examples include `mass` as particle weight, `splat` as collision flattening, `bounce` against static walkmeshes, `affectedbywind`, and unknown `blurlength`/`deadspace`. They are useful vocabulary, but Aurora runtime math still comes from decompilation and retail validation.
   - Local source confirms the UI reads the active or pinned `ParticleSettings`; therefore a `.blend` can carry Aurora VFX metadata even when no current object is being simulated.
   - Local evidence: `__init__.py:213`, `nvb_props.py:552-565`, `nvb_props.py:614-615`, `nvb_node.py:1120-1320`, `nvb_node.py:1249-1254`, `nvb_animnode.py:205-238`, `nvb_animnode.py:366-397`.

4. NeverBlender manual confirms Blender authoring constraints:
   - MDL classification includes `Effect` for visual effects.
   - Dummy nodes mark ground, impact, head, hand, and related spell/VFX attachment points.
   - Reference nodes appear in visual effects.
   - Emitter or incompatible animation data may be stored as text-like data rather than simulated.

5. NeverBlender's emitter UI is useful vocabulary, not a runtime spec.
   - The UI exposes `Fountain`, `Single`, `Explosion`, and `Lightning`; its Lightning description says a reference node is required.
   - The UI exposes `Loop` as a boolean with a `Single`-specific description, and the exporter mirrors that by writing `loop` only for `Single`. Treat this as authoring/schema confirmation for the Aurora source `+0x13c` field, not as Blender particle looping.
   - P2P UI exposes Bezier, Gravity, `p2p_bezier2`, `p2p_bezier3`, `src`, `target`, `combinetime`, `grav`, `drag`, and `threshold`.
   - NeverBlender labels `p2p_sel` values as `0` Undefined, `1` Bezier, and `2` Gravity, while NWN Wiki's author-facing notes/examples are not fully consistent. Import/export code must therefore preserve the raw selector and label provenance instead of trusting either external label as Aurora runtime truth.
   - The same UI/source leaves several Lightning descriptions as unknown (`???`), so it must not be used as proof of Lightning math.
   - Local evidence: `nvb_props.py:552-591`, `nvb_props.py:725-789`, `nvb_ui.py:1080-1108`.

6. Implementation consequence:
   - Use NeverBlender to validate field names, authoring UI vocabulary, and round-trip preservation.
   - Do not use Blender particle physics as the browser renderer algorithm.
   - If Blender import/export is added later, store Aurora emitter rows as custom properties plus raw preserved text/key/bezier-key/event blocks.
   - Any Blender viewport preview must be labelled non-canonical.
   - A correct browser renderer must be Aurora-owned: parse Aurora data first, then optionally expose a Blender-compatible authoring view.

7. Blender -> Aurora evidence matrix:
   - Allowed as primary implementation evidence:
     - Aurora decompilation fields, runtime branch behavior, and MDL/2DA resource contracts.
     - Retail NWN/NWN:EE runtime comparisons.
   - Allowed as secondary authoring evidence:
     - NeverBlender enum names, UI grouping, case-correction helpers, and import/export paths.
     - Official Blender API facts about where add-ons can store/keyframe data.
   - Allowed only as preview intuition:
     - Blender material alpha settings, Eevee transparency limitations, and particle viewport behavior.
   - Forbidden as runtime inference:
     - Blender `ParticleSettings.count`, frame ranges, cache/bake state, `physics_type`, `render_type`, emitter distribution, children, path/hair output, Geometry Nodes simulation state, object/collection instancing, point cache, and native evaluated particle state.
     - NeverBlender omissions, TODO labels, UI descriptions marked `???`, or export simplifications.
   - Required importer stance:
     - Normalize NeverBlender's split storage back into Aurora field names.
     - Preserve raw Aurora fields even when Blender cannot display or animate them.
     - Keep unsupported Blender previews behind explicit non-canonical diagnostics.

8. Blender authoring/import contract:
   - Treat Blender files as an optional authoring container for Aurora MDL source, not as the source format itself.
   - The only Blender-native particle settings that may round-trip directly are the fields NeverBlender explicitly uses as storage shims:
     - `normal_factor` -> Aurora `velocity`
     - `factor_random` -> Aurora `randvel`
     - `angular_velocity_factor` -> Aurora `particleRot`
   - Every other VFX field must be read from Aurora-named metadata (`settings.nvb`) or from the raw MDL/2DA source, with the raw source kept as the winner when there is disagreement.
   - A shared `ParticleSettings` data-block must be normalized per owning particle system/object, with shared-ID provenance. Do not mutate or cache it as a single Aurora emitter unless the Aurora node graph proves that one source node owns it.
   - If `settings.nvb` is unavailable because the NeverBlender add-on schema is missing, preserve Blender IDs and raw custom-property evidence where available, emit a schema-unavailable diagnostic, and do not synthesize absent Aurora fields from Blender defaults.
   - NeverBlender's imported emitter plane is an authoring handle derived from `xsize`/`ysize`; it is not a runtime quad, billboarding plane, collision plane, or particle spawn cache.
   - Blender `Object`/`Collection` particle instancing cannot become Aurora chunk rendering. Chunk rendering starts at Aurora `chunkName`, resolves an MDL resource, and owns particle lifetime/resource cleanup.
   - Blender particle cache, baked frames, edit mode, child particles, path data, or current viewport state must never populate Aurora active/free particle lists.
   - Blender material settings may generate preview materials, but only after the Aurora emitter `blend`, `renderorder`, `texture`, TXI, MTR, and shader-lane provenance have been preserved.
   - If a Blender-exported file omits a decompilation-confirmed Aurora emitter field, our importer must keep the missing field diagnostic separate from the raw Aurora source model. NeverBlender omissions are not deletion permission.
   - If a Blender-authored file contains custom properties outside NeverBlender's known schema, keep them as authoring metadata, not Aurora runtime state, until Aurora or retail evidence confirms the mapping.
   - For future Blender round-trip support, keep three payloads side by side:
     - `auroraRaw`: original MDL/2DA text, raw tokens, raw key/event/bezier blocks.
     - `auroraNormalized`: canonical Aurora field names, enums, numeric values, resource refs, and provenance.
     - `blenderAuthoring`: Blender object names, `ParticleSettings` IDs, F-Curves, UI state, and preview-only helpers.
   - Import/export comparison must detect these divergence classes:
     - raw Aurora field changed by Blender export
     - Blender preview field changed but Aurora raw field unchanged
     - NeverBlender split-storage mismatch (`velocity`/`randvel`/`particleRot`)
     - `chunkName`/`texture` conflict with `settings.nvb.particletype`
     - F-Curve timing converted through scene FPS
     - Blender Action slot/layer data not represented by legacy `action.fcurves`
     - unsupported `fieldbezierkey` or unknown event payload omitted by Blender
     - Blender material alpha changed without Aurora `blend` changing

9. Blender-source import decision tree:
   - If the input has Aurora MDL/2DA source, parse and preserve that as `auroraRaw` first; Blender/NeverBlender data can only annotate or propose edits.
   - If the input is a `.blend`/NeverBlender authoring file with no raw MDL payload, construct `auroraNormalized` only from `ParticleSettings.nvb` plus the approved native shims (`normal_factor`, `factor_random`, `angular_velocity_factor`) and emit a no-raw-source diagnostic.
   - If multiple object particle systems reference the same `ParticleSettings`, emit shared-settings provenance and build separate normalized emitter candidates per owning object/system only when the Aurora node/source context supports that split.
   - If a Blender Action uses slots/layers outside the legacy first-slot F-Curve view, keep that data as authoring metadata and emit an action-slot diagnostic rather than dropping it or pretending NeverBlender exported it.
   - Reject evaluated `ParticleSystem.particles`, `child_particles`, `point_cache`, baked cache, edit-mode state, and render-as object/collection output from canonical Aurora runtime construction.
   - Preserve Blender object names, particle-settings data-block names, scene FPS, render engine, material alpha settings, pinned-settings context, and F-Curves under `blenderAuthoring`.
   - When exporting back to Aurora, compare frame-derived seconds against original raw seconds with tolerance, and keep raw Aurora key/event/bezier tracks as the authority when present.
   - If a Blender-authored change affects only viewport preview state, report it as preview-only divergence rather than rewriting Aurora VFX behavior.
   - If a Blender-authored custom property is outside NeverBlender's known schema, keep it as `blenderAuthoring.unknownCustomProperty`, emit `VFX_BLENDER_UNKNOWN_CUSTOM_PROPERTY_AUTHORING_ONLY`, and do not promote it to runtime until Aurora or retail evidence proves it. If the property looks schema-like but lacks registered add-on/schema provenance, emit `VFX_BLENDER_IDPROPERTY_SCHEMA_PROVENANCE_REQUIRED`.

10. Blender-side validation fixtures:
   - Import a simple texture Fountain emitter such as local `backend/tmp_cot_fx01.mdl` and verify that Blender authoring state maps back to:
     - `update Fountain`
     - `render Billboard_to_World_Z`
     - `Blend Normal`
     - `spawnType 0`
     - atlas `xgrid 4`, `ygrid 4`, `fps 10`, `random 1`
     - `texture fxpa_smoke01`
   - Import a chunk emitter and verify `chunkName` drives the Aurora model-resource dependency even if `settings.nvb.particletype` is wrong or missing.
   - Import a P2P/Lightning fixture and verify child `node reference` presence is validated in the Aurora node graph, not inferred from Blender UI defaults.
   - Import an Explosion fixture with `event ... detonate` and verify event seconds and `detonate` survive raw-preserve even if Blender frame/F-Curve conversion is lossy.
   - Import a fixture with `fieldbezierkey` and verify Blender can be non-canonical while the Aurora parser still preserves the curve.
   - Import a Blender-authored emitter with keyed `ParticleSettings.nvb.birthrate` and native `ParticleSettings.normal_factor`; verify RNA data paths are recorded under `blenderAuthoring`, then normalized only through approved Aurora field mappings and never treated as Aurora runtime offsets.
   - Import two Blender particle systems sharing one `ParticleSettings` data-block; verify the importer records the shared settings ID and object/system owners, and does not collapse them into one Aurora emitter without source-node proof.
   - Import a Blender 4.4+ slotted/layered Action fixture; verify legacy first-slot F-Curves are not treated as full action coverage when additional slots/layers exist.
   - Import a `.blend` without the NeverBlender property schema available; verify missing `settings.nvb` values produce schema diagnostics, not Aurora default/runtime facts.
   - Import/export a Blender-authored Action containing an F-Curve modifier or sampled curve; verify the modifier/sample data is recorded as authoring metadata and does not replace Aurora direct/key/bezier-key evaluation.
   - Import/export a fixture with an unknown animated Aurora emitter field; verify the raw Aurora key block survives even if NeverBlender cannot expose or export it.
   - Export from Blender and compare against raw Aurora source with a field-level diff; do not rely on visual viewport parity as a round-trip test.
