## Current aurora-web Integration Blueprint

The next implementation pass should use the current project as an integration host, not as proof that VFX runtime already exists.

1. Existing MDL -> GLB converter boundary.
   - `backend/src/modules/runtime-settings/adapters/outbound/derived/aurora-mdl-ascii-to-glb.converter.ts` can provide useful parser examples for `node` scanning, texture reference capture, binary/ASCII detection, and GLB preview packaging.
   - Its `ParsedModel` shape keeps only `meshes` and `emitterTextureReferences`; it does not preserve full `node emitter` fields, active/free particle state, update families, render modes, animation controller targets, event scheduling, dependency edges, or effect-instance context.
   - `createEmitterProxyMesh()` creates a quad named `emitter_proxy` when an emitter-only model has texture references but no renderable mesh. That is a preview fallback and must emit `VFX_INTEGRATION_EMITTER_PROXY_PREVIEW_ONLY` / `VFX_GLB_EMITTER_PROXY_NON_CANONICAL` when used for VFX.
   - Do not extend this converter into the canonical VFX runtime. Add a separate VFX source/parser module that can reuse small helpers only after their lossiness is documented.
   - Local refs: `backend/src/modules/runtime-settings/adapters/outbound/derived/aurora-mdl-ascii-to-glb.converter.ts:181-219,760-786`; `backend/test/unit/aurora-mdl-ascii-to-glb.converter.spec.ts:54-62`.

2. Existing placeable 2DA helpers are not the VFX parser.
   - `parsePlaceableModelResrefsFromTwoDa()` returns only normalized model resrefs from `placeables.2da`.
   - `parsePlaceablesTwoDaRows()` drops rows without `ModelName` and returns only row ID, optional label, and normalized model resref.
   - That is correct for current placeable model enrichment, but forbidden for `visualeffects.2da`, `progfx.2da`, `spells.2da`, `iprp_visualfx.2da`, and `vfx_persistent.2da` because VFX source tables must preserve blank cells, quoted cells, unknown columns, sounds, phase refs, row/profile diagnostics, and unresolved resource refs.
   - VFX should start with a shared `AuroraTwoDaTable` parser plus typed readers. Any call to the placeable parser from VFX emits `VFX_INTEGRATION_PLACEABLE_2DA_PARSER_FORBIDDEN_FOR_VFX`.
   - Local refs: `backend/src/modules/runtime-settings/application/runtime-settings.application.service.ts:1366-1413`; `backend/src/modules/catalog/adapters/outbound/blob/module-snapshot-template-catalog.repository.ts:1125-1178`.

3. Runtime settings already contain VFX HAK evidence.
   - The active `lc_models` runtime-settings profile includes `lc_vfx.hak` and `cep3_vfx.hak`.
   - First VFX PRs must read the selected runtime-settings HAK profile and attach provenance to every resolved table/model/texture/sound dependency. Hardcoding `lc_vfx.hak`, scanning only vanilla, or ignoring profile HAK order is not acceptable.
   - Current runtime-settings source categories are `placeable`, `tile`, `area`, and `sound`; the schema, `RuntimeSourcesByAsset`, `RUNTIME_ASSET_KINDS`, cross-field validation, and resolved-HAK endpoint are built around those four categories. VFX must therefore not silently borrow the placeable policy just because `lc_models` happens to contain VFX HAK names.
   - The first VFX slice needs a dedicated VFX source category/profile, or an explicit temporary `AuroraVfxSourcePolicyAdapter` that records it is reusing `sources.placeable` as project evidence only. Missing that boundary emits `VFX_INTEGRATION_VFX_SOURCE_POLICY_REQUIRED` and `VFX_RESOURCE_RESOLVER_CATEGORY_SPLIT_REQUIRED`.
   - Resolved HAK input is implementation configuration, not retail precedence proof. `includeHaks`, `hakPriorityList`, `hakProfileId`, and the resulting `hakPaths` feed candidate traces and profile hashes; they do not let VFX label a winner as Aurora-retail-correct without selected-client validation. Violations emit `VFX_INTEGRATION_RUNTIME_SETTINGS_NOT_RETAIL_PRECEDENCE`.
   - Every VFX resolve result must carry runtime-settings revision, source category, HAK mode (`disabled | inline | profile | none`), selected profile ID or inline-list marker, ordered HAK list hash, selected source layer, source table/resource hash, and lower-precedence candidates. Cache keys that omit the HAK/profile component emit `VFX_INTEGRATION_HAK_PROFILE_HASH_REQUIRED` or `VFX_RESOURCE_CACHE_KEY_HAK_PROFILE_REQUIRED`.
   - Winning `visualeffects.2da`, `progfx.2da`, `vfx_persistent.2da`, `spells.2da`, MDL, texture, TXI, MTR, shader, sound, TLK, and script resources are single-source selections. A row or cell from a lower-precedence table cannot be merged into the selected table unless a profile-specific 2DA merge tool has produced a new resolved source artifact with its own hash; otherwise emit `VFX_RESOURCE_SOURCE_LAYER_MERGE_FORBIDDEN` / `VFX_RESOURCE_SELECTED_TABLE_HASH_REQUIRED`.
   - Runtime `benchmarkCandidates.placeableHeavyVfx` and `placeableVfxPlcAlternative` are fixture selection and smoke-test hints, not VFX source profiles. Using them to infer HAK order, source precedence, or canonical visualeffects rows emits `VFX_BENCHMARK_CANDIDATE_NOT_SOURCE_PROFILE`.
   - The current project docs define resolver policy in draft/final contracts, but the VFX path must check whether a callable implementation exists. If not, the first VFX slice needs a minimal resolver facade or explicit blocker diagnostic instead of ad hoc file searches.
   - Local refs: `backend/config/runtime-settings.json:45-89`; `backend/docs/config/runtime-settings.md:29-74`; `backend/src/modules/runtime-settings/domain/runtime-settings.types.ts:31-38`; `backend/src/modules/runtime-settings/domain/runtime-settings.schema.ts:86-90,133-144`; `backend/src/modules/runtime-settings/application/runtime-settings.application.service.ts:39,824-838,1271-1281`; `backend/docs/aurora-reverse/code-skeleton-source-resolver-r68.md`; `backend/docs/aurora-reverse/resolver-interfaces-contract-r69.md`; `backend/docs/aurora-reverse/resource-precedence-matrix-r65.md`.

4. Source precedence must be recorded as selected project policy plus external comparison risk.
   - Project R65 says models/textures/2DA/TLK use `module_decompiled -> module_packed -> hak -> override -> vanilla KEY/BIF`, while the resolver skeleton often shortens this to `module_decompiled -> module_packed -> hak -> vanilla`.
   - External NWN community documentation says override replaces core resources but is replaced by module or HAK resources, and the top HAK method exists because the highest HAK can carry merged 2DA rows; NWN Wiki also warns that `visualeffects.2da` is a client/server visual table with row-ID limits.
   - Therefore VFX must not silently claim exact retail resource parity from the project policy alone. Every VFX resolve result needs policy ID/version, candidate trace, source layer winner, and a `VFX_RESOLVER_PRECEDENCE_RUNTIME_UNVERIFIED` diagnostic when HAK/module/override conflicts matter.
   - External sources: https://nwn.fandom.com/wiki/Override, https://nwn.wiki/spaces/NWN1/pages/38174875/2da%2BFiles, https://neverwintervault.org/project/nwn1/other/hakpack-and-2da-merging-tutorial

5. Frontend VFX lane is preserve/preview only until a structured payload exists.
   - `SceneObjectVfxPreservePayload` currently stores `profile`, `emitter`, `script`, `flags`, and `extra` as a placeholder.
   - `createPlaceableVfxPreviewGroup()` creates procedural Three.js spheres/sprites/scaffolds from heuristics. It is useful for editor affordance, but it is not Aurora particle update/render behavior and it is not Blender particle-system behavior.
   - `workspaceObjectMeshLayer` chooses between render package GLB, primitive fallback, and the VFX preview group. This selection must remain a preview lane until backend sends a structured `AuroraVfxPayload` with source rows, effect-instance context, dependency graph, diagnostics, and schema version.
   - The first structured frontend upgrade should add payload schema versioning and diagnostic badges before adding canonical particle rendering. Current sprite output should label itself with `VFX_INTEGRATION_FRONTEND_SPRITE_PREVIEW_ONLY`.
   - Current backend processing graph already has `GraphResourceNodeKind = "vfx_preset"` and builds those nodes from template `metadata.vfxPreset` values such as `torch_smoke_soft`. This is project catalog/resource-graph metadata, not a `visualeffects.2da` row ID, not a `ProgFX_*` source row, and not an `EffectVisualEffect()` constructor argument.
   - Treat `vfx_preset` nodes as dependency/preview/catalog hints until they are linked to a structured `AuroraVfxPayload` with source-row provenance. Promoting them to source rows, phase schedules, or effect instances emits `VFX_PROCESSING_GRAPH_VFX_PRESET_NOT_VISUALEFFECTS_ROW`, `VFX_CURRENT_VFX_PRESET_RESOURCE_NODE_PREVIEW_ONLY`, or `VFX_CATALOG_VFXPRESET_METADATA_NOT_PHASE_SOURCE`.
   - Public check: NWN Lexicon documents `EffectVisualEffect()` as using `visualeffects.2da`; NWN Wiki describes `visualeffects.2da` as the table called by the game or `EffectVisualEffect`. Therefore current project preset strings must stay separate from row-number provenance.

## Aurora-Blender Authoring Adapter Matrix

This matrix is for future Blender/NeverBlender import/export support. It is not a renderer plan.

1. Payload separation is mandatory.
   - Every Blender-facing conversion should produce at least four lanes:
     - `auroraRaw`: original MDL/2DA/source rows, unknown fields, raw key rows, raw event rows, and source offsets.
     - `auroraNormalized`: typed Aurora emitter/source/effect records with Ghidra/source provenance.
     - `blenderAuthoring`: Blender objects, particle settings, F-Curves, actions, UI defaults, and NeverBlender carrier paths.
     - `blenderPreview`: optional viewport/material/simulation output, always non-canonical.
   - Do not let `blenderAuthoring` or `blenderPreview` overwrite `auroraRaw` when NeverBlender omits a field or stores it differently.

2. NeverBlender emitter carrier model.
   - Import creates a Blender mesh object for the emitter plane, sets `hide_render = True`, adds a `PARTICLE_SYSTEM`, writes known emitter fields to `ParticleSettings.nvb` or native particle settings, and sets `ParticleSettings.count = 0`.
   - This proves a metadata-carrier pattern, not a running Blender particle simulation.
   - Official Blender `ParticleSettings` docs describe the settings block as reusable by multiple particle systems. Therefore importer output must record all owner object/system references and must not assume one `ParticleSettings` data-block equals one Aurora source emitter.
   - Official Blender `ParticleSystem` docs expose generated `particles`, `child_particles`, `point_cache`, `seed`, and `settings`. These are Blender runtime/simulation surfaces and must be ignored for canonical Aurora active/free particle lists.
   - Local refs: `.codex-tmp/neverblender_40-010/neverblender/nvb_node.py:1172-1224`; `.codex-tmp/neverblender_40-010/neverblender/nvb_node.py:1222-1327`.
   - Sources: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.ParticleSettings.html, https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.ParticleSystem.html

3. Field storage matrix.
   - NeverBlender `Emitter.property_dict` maps most Aurora MDL emitter fields to `ParticleSettings.nvb.*`: `update`, `loop`, `render`, `blend`, `spawntype`, `renderorder`, `birthrate`, `lifeexp`, `mass`, `spread`, `splat`, `affectedbywind`, colors, alpha, size, bounce, blur/deadspace, texture/chunk/atlas, P2P, blast, lightning, and inheritance fields.
   - Three fields intentionally use native Blender particle settings: `velocity -> ParticleSettings.normal_factor`, `randvel -> ParticleSettings.factor_random`, and `particlerot -> ParticleSettings.angular_velocity_factor`.
   - Those native fields are authoring shims only. Official Blender docs define them as Blender particle-system velocity/rotation controls, while Aurora decompilation owns the runtime reset, spread, inheritance, and velocity slots.
   - Local refs: `.codex-tmp/neverblender_40-010/neverblender/nvb_node.py:1070-1124`; `.codex-tmp/neverblender_40-010/neverblender/nvb_props.py:552-807`.
   - Source: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.ParticleSettings.html

4. Texture/chunk lane matrix.
   - `texture`, `twosidedtex`, `m_istinted`, `xgrid`, `ygrid`, `fps`, `framestart`, `frameend`, and `random` live under `ParticleSettings.nvb` and export only when a texture value is present in NeverBlender.
   - `chunkname` exports when non-empty and not `null`. It remains the Aurora chunk-model lane, not a Blender object/collection particle renderer.
   - NeverBlender has a UI field `particletype`, but the inspected import code uses comparison expressions (`==`) rather than assignment when trying to infer it from `chunkname`. Therefore `particletype` is UI/authoring evidence only; lane selection must use raw Aurora `chunkName` and `texture`.
   - Local refs: `.codex-tmp/neverblender_40-010/neverblender/nvb_node.py:1172-1187`; `.codex-tmp/neverblender_40-010/neverblender/nvb_node.py:1271-1292`.

5. Emitter size matrix.
   - NeverBlender parses `xsize`/`ysize` as emitter mesh size in centimeters and builds a hidden Blender plane with `xsize / 100` and `ysize / 100` dimensions.
   - Export writes `xsize`/`ysize` from `obj.dimensions.x * 100` and `obj.dimensions.y * 100`.
   - This is an authoring-plane bridge only. It must not become Aurora particle draw geometry, collision geometry, a texture quad, or a Blender emission-source proof.
   - Local refs: `.codex-tmp/neverblender_40-010/neverblender/nvb_node.py:1138-1160`; `.codex-tmp/neverblender_40-010/neverblender/nvb_node.py:1188-1201`; `.codex-tmp/neverblender_40-010/neverblender/nvb_node.py:1241-1242`.

6. Animation/key matrix.
   - NeverBlender imports emitter animation by creating F-Curves on `part_sys.settings`; custom properties are grouped under `Aurora Emitter`.
   - Export reads object keys and particle-settings animation data, then writes normal `fieldkey` lists from F-Curve keyframes.
   - In the inspected source, no broad `fieldbezierkey` export path exists. That is a NeverBlender limitation, not Aurora evidence.
   - Official Blender `Action.fcurves` is a legacy first-slot API in current docs; Blender 4.4+ layered/slotted actions require version/slot provenance. F-Curve evaluation, sampled points, modifiers, mute/valid state, and extrapolation are Blender authoring facts, not Aurora evaluator proof.
   - Local refs: `.codex-tmp/neverblender_40-010/neverblender/nvb_animnode.py:208-227`; `.codex-tmp/neverblender_40-010/neverblender/nvb_animnode.py:516-538`.
   - Sources: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.Action.html, https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.FCurve.html

7. Event/FPS matrix.
   - NeverBlender imports MDL animation `event <time> <name>` rows into an event list by converting seconds to frames with scene FPS.
   - Export converts event frames back to seconds with `(event.frame - anim.frameStart) / fps` and rounds to three decimals.
   - Aurora `detonate` event behavior must still be driven by Aurora event scanning/runtime evidence. Blender FPS conversion is round-trip metadata and needs tolerance/provenance diagnostics.
   - Local refs: `.codex-tmp/neverblender_40-010/neverblender/nvb_anim.py:31-42`; `.codex-tmp/neverblender_40-010/neverblender/nvb_anim.py:138-142`.

8. Cache/runtime matrix.
   - Blender point caches are physics-simulation caches with frame ranges and baked/outdated states. They are not Aurora constructor state, source emitter defaults, active/free lists, particle age, or Motion_Blur previous-position slots.
   - NeverBlender UI may use particle-system/cache/editability state to decide whether a panel is editable. Treat that as an authoring UI gate only.
   - Local ref: `.codex-tmp/neverblender_40-010/neverblender/nvb_ui.py:925-975`.
   - Source: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.PointCache.html

9. Official Blender VFX/particle semantics boundary.
   - Blender's native particle model is split between reusable `ParticleSettings` data-blocks and object-owned `ParticleSystem` runtime wrappers. The API exposes generated `particles`, `child_particles`, `point_cache`, `seed`, `settings`, owner object links, and per-system vertex groups; none of these are Aurora source-emitter offsets, source flags, or active/free particle arrays.
   - Blender emission/timing controls (`count`, start/end frames, lifetime, lifetime randomness, seed, distribution source) are Blender simulation inputs. They do not map to Aurora `birthrate`, `lifeExp`, `loop`, or detonate events unless NeverBlender or raw MDL source explicitly supplies the Aurora field row.
   - Blender velocity controls describe initial speed through normal, tangent, object axes, object velocity, and randomization. NeverBlender's `velocity -> normal_factor` and `randvel -> factor_random` shims are useful for authoring/export, but Aurora reset/update code still owns final velocity, spread, inherit flags, mass, P2P, bounce, and wind behavior.
   - Blender Newtonian particles use animator-selected integrators, Brownian motion, drag, dampening, timestep/subframes, and deflection. Keyed, Boids, Fluid, No Physics, and child-particle systems are separate Blender physics families; they must never be normalized into Aurora `update` values such as `Fountain`, `Single`, `Explosion`, `Lightning`, `Linked`, or `Motion_Blur`.
   - Blender force fields are external effectors with field weights, group filters, global gravity weight, per-effector `FieldSettings`, and cache invalidation concerns. Even a Blender `Wind` effector or `EffectorWeights.wind` value is not Aurora `affectedByWind`, `SetAreaWind`, or Explosion `blastRadius/blastLength`; Aurora uses the recovered wind manager and point-source records.
   - Blender point caches are frame-windowed bake/memory/disk/external simulation caches, calculated only within the cache frame envelope and protected after baking. They cannot prove Aurora runtime state, cache resets, per-particle reuse, previous-position slots, or animation-event consumption.
   - Blender time is frame-based authoring/evaluation state. Scene `fps`/`fps_base`, `frame_set`, `frame_current_final`, timeline preview ranges, simulation cache ranges, Geometry Nodes simulation clock, and depsgraph/evaluated state are adapter evidence only; Aurora source rows keep seconds/key-time/event-time provenance until an explicit conversion record exists.
   - Blender render modes (`None`, `Halo`, `Path`, `Object`, `Collection`) and object/collection instancing are visual/rendering choices. They are not Aurora emitter `render`, `blend`, `texture`, `chunkName`, atlas, render-order, or chunk-model semantics; `Render As Object/Collection` may be preview-only for chunks, never canonical chunk rendering.
   - Blender child particles are derived visualization/simulation children of parent particles; changing child counts can avoid recalculating parent physics. Aurora has no equivalent child-particle multiplier in the recovered emitter runtime, so child particles are preview metadata only.
   - Official sources: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.ParticleSettings.html, https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.ParticleSystem.html, https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.PointCache.html, https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.EffectorWeights.html, https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.FieldSettings.html
   - Official time/evaluation sources: https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.Scene.html, https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.RenderSettings.html, https://docs.blender.org/api/current/bpy.types.Depsgraph.html, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/editors/timeline.html, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/physics/baking.html, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/simulation/simulation_zone.html, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/modeling/geometry_nodes/baking.html
   - Official manual sources: https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/physics/particles/emitter/emission.html, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/physics/particles/emitter/velocity.html, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/physics/particles/emitter/physics/newtonian.html, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/physics/particles/emitter/force_field.html, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/physics/particles/emitter/cache.html, https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/physics/particles/emitter/render.html

## Required VFX Domain Contract

The implementation must preserve at least:

1. Source row data:
   - `visualeffects.2da` row ID
   - `Type_FD`
   - Aurora/NWN1 impact and cessation model refs
   - preserved custom/cross-profile columns such as `Dur_*_Node`
   - `ProgFX_*` refs
   - sound refs
   - low-quality/low-violence fallback refs

2. Item-property visual source data:
   - separate `iprp_visualfx.2da` source identity
   - item-property subtype ID
   - `ModelSuffix` raw cell and resolved suffix
   - suffix provenance: source table versus Aurora hardcoded fallback
   - item-property computed suffix provenance for local `iprp_damagecost`/`iprp_meleecost`/hardcoded-property routines
   - `sourceKind`, source table name, local routine anchor, property type/subtype/cost/param evidence, table-gate result, and selected profile
   - known fallback suffix family: `_fxacid`, `_fxfrost`, `_fxelect`, `_fxfire`, `_fxsonic`, `_fxholy`, `_fxneg`
   - damage-style suffix mapping provenance: `6 -> _fxacid`, `7 -> _fxfrost`, `9 -> _fxelect`, `10 -> _fxfire`, `13 -> _fxsonic`
   - holy/negative suffix mapping provenance from the local item-property routines
   - explicit diagnostic boundary from `visualeffects.2da`, `Type_FD`, phase slots, and `EffectVisualEffect`

3. Area-of-effect persistent source/instance data:
   - separate `vfx_persistent.2da` source identity
   - AOE row ID in the `vfx_persistent.2da` namespace, explicitly not a `visualeffects.2da` row ID
   - `LABEL` as the AOE object tag/source label when supported by the selected profile
   - shape footprint fields such as `SHAPE`, `RADIUS`, `WIDTH`, and `LENGTH`, preserved with schema provenance
   - event script refs: OnEnter, OnHeartbeat, OnExit, and user-defined/event-script support when profile evidence supplies it
   - visual footprint refs such as `DurationVFX`, `MODEL01..MODEL03`, low-quality model alternates, model counts/durations, and edge weights, all preserved as AOE-row data rather than normal VFX phase slots
   - AOE sound refs preserved as sound/event resources, not model refs
   - AOE application context: static location versus mobile/followed object, duration type, requested duration, creator/effect creator provenance, spell/caster metadata when observable, and object lookup/destruction provenance
   - local decompilation absence of direct `vfx_persistent`/`EffectAreaOfEffect` symbols recorded before treating external schema as runtime proof

4. Spell/toolset visual source data:
   - separate `spells.2da` source identity and physical spell row ID
   - raw spell label/name cells, raw cell map, source layer, schema/profile evidence, and row diagnostics
   - visual/model refs such as `ConjHeadVisual`, `ConjHandVisual`, `ConjGrndVisual`, `CastHeadVisual`, `CastHandVisual`, `CastGrndVisual`, and `ProjModel`, each with requested resource class and owner-column provenance
   - projectile context such as `Proj`, `ProjType`, `ProjSpwnPoint`, `ProjOrientation`, `HasProjectile`, and profile-specific MIRV/projectile fields when present
   - script refs such as `ImpactScript`, `BardImpactScript`, and `MirvImpactScript` preserved as script resources, not VFX/model resources
   - sound refs such as `ProjSound`, `ConjSoundVFX`, `CastSound`, and profile variants preserved as sound resources
   - `AuroraSpellProjectilePresentationRequest` data for spell/action projectile previews, including caster/source object, target object/location, call mode, projectile path/orientation/spawn-point policy, and fake-vs-real script policy
   - `AuroraSpellProjectileProgFxBridge` data when an EE/profile-gated `progfx.2da` Type 10/11 request links back to a spell row or spell projectile payload
   - local string-cluster provenance for `projectile`, `visfx`, `visualeffect`, `fxground`, `fximpact`, `fxhead`, `fxbeam`, `fxfail`, `conjurevisual`, `conjuregroundvisual`, and `castvisual`
   - explicit diagnostic boundary from `visualeffects.2da`, `EffectVisualEffect`, `EffectBeam`, `BODY_NODE_*`, `ProgFX_*`, MDL emitter fields, and Blender particle settings

5. Effect instance data:
   - constructed effect kind: visual effect, beam, or unknown
   - external/observed effect type where available, e.g. `EFFECT_TYPE_VISUALEFFECT` or `EFFECT_TYPE_BEAM`
   - optional NWScript function provenance: function name, VM function ID when known from a script table, source authority (`ghidra`, `xoreos`, `lexicon`, `beamdog`, `retailFixture`), and whether the body/constructor implementation is actually recovered

## Do Not Guess

Do not guess these as canonical until Aurora/decomp/retail evidence proves them:

1. Exact blend equations for `Lighten`/mode `2` and `Punch-Through`.
   - `Punch-Through` is decompilation string evidence.
   - `Lighten` is NeverBlender/NWN Wiki author-facing evidence, but not a literal in the targeted Aurora emitter string table.
   - Mode `2` is a raw fallback bucket for every non-normal/non-punch literal; do not rename unknown raw literals to `Lighten`.
   - The current C export shows the same visible non-punch state wrapper sequence for mode `0` and mode `2`, so any final `Lighten` distinction remains capture-gated.
   - Aurora render-state wrappers, depth-write differences, inferred state roles, and shader variant selection are mapped.
   - Exact `glBlendFunc` factors still need shader/retail/GPU capture verification.
2. Particle sort order and alpha ordering edge cases.
   - `renderorder` is mapped as a source-emitter short and appears in the runtime draw-item comparator as a tie-breaker after an earlier depth/sort key.
   - NWN Wiki documents lower `renderorder` values as higher priority, but exact final over/under behavior still depends on surrounding sort direction, blend/depth lanes, chunk emitters, and category grouping.
   - NeverBlender's `renderorder min=0`, Blender transparent-material sorting, and Three.js `Object3D.renderOrder` are authoring/preview/adapter facts, not Aurora runtime range or queue semantics.
   - No per-particle camera sort was found in the inspected textured-particle vertex builder; do not invent one for alpha correctness.
3. Exact collision resolver identity and walkmesh parity.
   - The bounce branch, normal reflection, `bounce_co` scaling, settled-particle flag, and splat render-state interaction are mapped.
   - The exact collision-query vtable target, walkmesh/static-object inclusion policy, full query-helper struct layout, and final visual parity for `splat` still need retail capture or deeper struct recovery. Chunk-model list setup and the visible size-extent/post-hit nudge lane are mapped enough to require diagnostics.
   - `surfacemat.2da`/walkmesh surface material evidence is now treated as optional collision-surface context. The unresolved part is whether the Aurora particle collision service filters by material row, `Walk`, `WalkCheck`, mesh kind, or a separate collision class table.
   - `threshold` is mapped as a P2P/gravity arrival/expiration radius, not as generic surface collision.
4. Wind integration details beyond the mapped shared wind-manager calls.
   - `affectedByWind` and Explosion `blastRadius`/`blastLength` both reach the global wind manager.
   - The point-source record shape is now recovered from the local decompilation, but retail force scaling, visual decay parity, global wind variation/noise math, and exact client/server authority for wind still need runtime validation.
5. P2P gravity/bezier math.
   - Aurora parser and runtime prove the fields and reference-target topology.
   - Lightning-compatible segment count now has local runtime evidence through evaluated slot `+0x58`, but the public `subdivision` authoring label remains an external/profile alias candidate because no local parser string was recovered.
   - Gravity overshoot, Bezier handles, exact random distribution, and final Lightning jitter naming still need retail fixtures or deeper helper naming.
   - A non-canonical preview may draw a reference-linked chain only if diagnostics say the canonical runtime is incomplete.
6. Exact render-mode orientation math for all edge cases.
   - IDs, mode-specific basis families, endpoint topology, landed/splat basis selection, and softness gating are mapped from the vertex builder.
   - `Motion_Blur` previous-position blending, `blurlength` offset, and missing-token default `1.0f` are mapped, but zero/negative `blurlength` behavior and exact family-update ordering still need selected source data or retail proof.
   - `particleRot` runtime state advance and `+/- 2*pi` wrap are mapped, but source authoring-unit conversion remains profile-gated because external docs describe rotations-per-second while the visible Aurora update adds the evaluated slot directly to a radians-like wrapped state.
   - Exact quaternion slot names, handedness labels, camera matrix naming, and pixel-level retail parity still require struct recovery or targeted runtime comparison.
7. Particle overflow/caps and emitter culling.
   - Active/free pointer-list capacity growth is mapped: empty lists grow to `0x10`, then double. This proves storage growth behavior, not a fixed visual cap.
   - Textured draw-buffer growth is mapped separately: the shared vertex buffer expands until it can hold `drawParticleCount * 6` vertices. Do not confuse draw-buffer capacity with emitter spawn policy.
   - A targeted local search did not expose a `maxParticles`/`maxparticles` emitter token in this decompilation export. Do not invent one for browser performance or UI convenience.
   - `Single` max-one-active and Lightning exact segment-count reconciliation are family-specific runtime rules. They are not a global cap for Fountain, Explosion, trail, or chunk emitters.
   - NWN Wiki's apparent `500cm x 500cm` emitter-size cap is external authoring evidence. It does not prove an active-particle-count cap and does not override Aurora's local spawn-rectangle/reset path until retail comparison confirms the selected profile.
   - Local `bboxMin`/`bboxMax` strings prove bounding-box vocabulary exists, but the current C export does not expose a trusted emitter-culling call site. Preserve bounding fields and retail/debug evidence, but do not add canonical frustum/viewport culling without deeper runtime proof.

   - `particleSoftness` is mapped as the particle path's computed softness scalar written through float-uniform slot `0`, with mode/size/splat gates and a max-half-extent size accumulator.

    - Aurora parser evidence proves `colorMid`, `percentStart`, `percentMid`, `percentEnd`, `alphaMid`, `sizeMid`, and `sizeMid_y` exist and can have direct/key/bezier-key data.
    - The visible parser block proves target offsets for preservation: `alphaMid` -> `0x1d4`, `colorMid` -> `0x1d8`, `percentStart` -> `0x1e4`, `percentMid` -> `0x1e5`, `percentEnd` -> `0x1e6`, `sizeMid` -> `0x1e8`, and `sizeMid_y` -> `0x1ec`.
    - The byte-adjacent `percent*` offsets are storage/layout evidence only. Do not infer percent units, normalization, or age-curve breakpoints from adjacency alone.
    - The inspected textured-particle renderer proves start/end age interpolation, but not a mid-point or percent-segment ramp.
    - Preserve and evaluate the fields as source/controller data, but do not invent a piecewise age curve, Blender color ramp, or authoring-tool interpretation until the Aurora runtime use is located or captured.
18. Whether a PoC or Three.js preview formula is canonical.
    - `Areas Generator 3d` contains a useful VFX runtime prototype and diagnosis report, but it uses heuristic scales, density multipliers, texture aliases, local overrides, Three.js material blending, and mid-curve formulas that are not automatically Aurora evidence.
    - Current `aurora-web` frontend VFX sprites/scaffolds are UX previews keyed by metadata/fingerprint, not Aurora `node emitter` execution.
    - Treat every PoC/Three formula as suspect until matched to decompilation or retail capture.
19. Exact `vfx_persistent.2da` runtime behavior.
    - External docs provide the table role, event scripts, object identity, shape fields, and visual/sound footprint fields, but the targeted local decompilation export did not expose `vfx_persistent` or `EffectAreaOfEffect`.
    - Do not guess exact AOE heartbeat cadence, mobile update frequency, shape inclusion math, random spawned-model placement, `DurationVFX` playback lifetime, sound loop/cessation timing, creator metadata propagation, dispel/destruction ordering, or low-quality fallback branch.
    - Local `ONHEARTBEAT` strings are generic event vocabulary, not proof of AOE table schema or timing.
    - Do not model AOE persistence by extending `EffectVisualEffect`, `ProgFX_Duration`, Blender particle cache lifetime, or a permanent Three.js scene child.
20. Exact `spells.2da` visual/projectile runtime mapping.
    - External docs provide column names and broad meanings for spell visual, sound, script, animation, and projectile slots, while local decompilation proves table bootstrap and lower-case slot vocabulary.
    - Do not guess whether a `Conj*Visual`, `Cast*Visual`, `ProjModel`, `fxground`, `fximpact`, `fxhead`, `fxbeam`, `fxfail`, `visfx`, or `visualeffect` source slot is a `visualeffects.2da` row ID, an MDL model resref, a toolset-only value, or a profile-specific lookup without owning-table schema evidence.
    - Do not guess projectile/MIRV travel timing, spawn-node mapping, target-facing orientation, or damage/impact synchronization from `ProjType`, `ProjSpwnPoint`, `ProjOrientation`, or `ProgFX` Type 10 docs alone.
    - Do not treat `ImpactScript`/`BardImpactScript`/`MirvImpactScript` as VFX resources, or spell sound slots as model resources.
    - Do not let `.sef`/`ProjSEF`-style cells enter the Aurora/NWN1 runtime path unless an explicit SEF-capable profile is selected.
21. Exact TXI/MTR/custom-shader effect on canonical particle emitters.
    - Local decompilation proves particle shader entrypoints, emitter `texture`, mesh/material `materialname`, and MTR/TXI/SHD resource vocabulary, but it does not prove that an MTR custom shader or TXI procedural directive changes emitter `update`, `render`, `blend`, active/free list, atlas stepping, or particle spawn math.
    - Preserve TXI/MTR/SHD dependencies and show them in diagnostics, but keep them out of canonical particle simulation until recovered call-sites or retail fixtures prove the exact lane.
    - EE notes about PLT VFX textures, spawned-model fog/self-illumination, alpha mean, and custom shader relinking are profile facts, not classic Aurora defaults.

## Implementation Sequence

Recommended order:

1. Parser preservation first.
   - Add/extend MDL ASCII/binary parser contracts for `node emitter`.
   - Record local Ghidra function anchors and role confidence for every parser/runtime claim that depends on decompilation evidence.
   - Add shared animated-track support for direct values, `fieldkey`, and `fieldbezierkey`.
   - Preserve key row source text, component counts, converted orientation values, and animation events.
   - Define the shared Aurora animation evaluation pass before renderer work: value pool plus metadata records, target-object/target-offset writes, blend weight, event scan order, and source-live-read timing.
   - Preserve unknown fields and raw text slices.
   - Add tests for all known fields plus unknown field round-trip.

2. 2DA-driven VFX source model.
   - Add a generic source-preserving 2DA parser before any VFX-specific typed reader.
   - Preserve physical row index, displayed first-column token, header map, raw cells, quoted/blank-cell state, source layer, and selected winner file.
   - Do not reuse the existing `placeables.2da` parser as the VFX parser; it intentionally drops rows without `ModelName`.
   - Parse `visualeffects.2da`.
   - Link `ProgFX_*` to optional `progfx.2da`.
   - Keep line ID and `Type_FD` explicit.
   - Keep Aurora/NWN1 impact model refs, cessation model refs, sounds, fallback refs, and `ProgFX_*` phase slots separate.
   - Preserve unknown/custom columns such as `Dur_*_Node`, but emit profile diagnostics instead of treating them as Aurora/NWN1 model slots.
   - Preserve `.sef` references as raw source data with unsupported-profile diagnostics for Aurora/NWN1.
   - Keep `iprp_visualfx.2da` as a separate item-property lookup table.
   - Preserve `iprp_visualfx` `ModelSuffix` and Aurora hardcoded suffix fallback provenance separately from normal VFX phase/resource diagnostics.
   - Add `AuroraSpellVisualSourceRow` or equivalent for `spells.2da` visual/projectile/script/sound slots, with owner-column provenance and requested resource class.
   - Preserve `spells.2da` projectile context separately from MDL emitter fields, `visualeffects.2da` phases, and `EffectBeam` context.
   - Keep `vfx_persistent.2da` as a separate AOE/persistent-effect table with row IDs, event scripts, shape footprint, visual model/sound footprint, and application context separated from normal `visualeffects.2da` phase rows.
   - Preserve `vfx_persistent.2da` schema as external/profile evidence in this report, because the targeted local decompilation export does not expose direct `vfx_persistent` table strings.
   - Parse `progfx.2da` as an EE/profile-gated typed table with raw `Param1..Param8` preservation before adding typed renderer behavior.
   - Keep Type 7 beams, Type 10 MIRVs, Type 12 node-attached VFX, Type 4 light priority, Type 8 delete-model, and Type 9 hardcoded chunks out of generic emitter preview code.

3. Effect-entry contract.
   - Preserve row ID, constructed effect kind, application mode, duration mode, miss flag, and EE transform tuple.
   - Preserve optional NWScript function-name/function-ID provenance from xoreos or script fixtures, but mark xoreos function-table entries as name/index evidence unless a runtime body is recovered.
   - Preserve `GetEffect*` observation slots as profile-gated external/retail evidence, not as classic Aurora source fields.
   - Preserve observable effect parameter slots where available, without over-naming unverified beam indices.
   - Preserve beam source object, target context, and beam body-node anchor.
   - Keep beam body nodes separate from creature appearance `BodyPart_*`/`CREATURE_PART_*` data.
   - Preserve `GetEffectCreator`/creator provenance separately from applying object and beam `oEffector`.
   - Keep mesh `beaming` and spell/toolset `fxbeam` slots as preserved upstream metadata, not runtime beam constructors.
   - Treat `Type_FD` as the duration/instant gate before renderer scheduling.
   - Treat `EffectAreaOfEffect` as a separate constructed effect kind with AOE row ID, static/mobile context, creator provenance, event scripts, and pseudo-object/runtime-object state.
   - Do not let normal `ApplyEffectAtLocation` VFX scheduling synthesize AOE persistence unless the constructed effect is explicitly `EffectAreaOfEffect`.

3.1. Runtime function-anchor contract.
   - Store constructor/tick separation for VFX runtime families. `FUN_00a31240`-style constructor anchors and `FUN_00a31288`-style tick anchors are different evidence.
   - Preserve `sourceOffset` and `runtimeOffset` separately. Source MDL fields, evaluated controller targets, and live runtime particle fields can share names but are not the same storage.
   - Keep all friendly class names such as Fountain/Explosion/Single/Lightning-compatible as aliases with Ghidra provenance until recovered symbols or retail traces validate them.

4. Resource resolver.
   - Resolve model refs, textures, TXI, MTR, shaders, and chunk MDLs through existing HAK/resource precedence.
   - Use the shared resolver interface and record policy ID/version, candidate trace, winner layer, and unresolved diagnostics.
   - Read the selected runtime-settings HAK profile before resolving VFX resources; the current `lc_models` profile includes `lc_vfx.hak` and `cep3_vfx.hak`, so a vanilla-only first pass is knowingly incomplete.
   - If `processing/source-resolver` is still only a documented contract, add a minimal VFX resolver facade or emit `VFX_INTEGRATION_SOURCE_RESOLVER_MODULE_NOT_READY`; do not replace it with direct filename scans inside VFX parsers.
   - Keep raw resref, normalized lookup key, requested resource class, and source field path together in `AuroraVfxResourceRef`.
   - Build an `AuroraVfxDependencyGraph` with explicit parent/child edges before renderer work; flat resource arrays are insufficient for VFX.
   - Preserve lane roles for phase model, spawned model, emitter texture, chunk model, TXI sidecar, MTR material, MTR texture slot, material custom shader, particle shader, beam-volume shader, and spell/toolset refs.
   - Emit lane-collapse diagnostics when `texture`, `texture0`, `materialname`, `chunkName`, shader names, or TXI directives are treated as interchangeable strings.
   - Diagnose HAK/module precedence conflicts as runtime-unverified until retail comparison proves the selected policy matches Aurora.
   - Treat `chunkName` as a model resref, not as a texture.
   - Emit diagnostics for unresolved refs.

5. DTO/frontend preserve contract.
   - Upgrade `vfxPayload` from placeholder to structured preserve-first contract.
   - Include schema version, source-row provenance, effect-instance context, dependency graph references, diagnostics, and compatibility/preserve buckets.
   - Keep the existing Three.js sprite/scaffold group and GLB `emitter_proxy` as explicitly non-canonical preview adapters until backend canonical payloads and runtime tests exist.
   - Keep `vfx` as `Placeable List` subtype unless future Aurora evidence proves a separate GIT family.
   - Keep placeable VFX classification as catalog/scene-object evidence, not as `EffectVisualEffect` construction. Label/resref pattern matches emit `VFX_PLACEABLE_KIND_NOT_EFFECTVISUALEFFECT` if promoted to a `visualeffects.2da` row without a row ID source.
   - Scene VFX placeable anchors emit `VFX_SCENE_PLACEABLE_VFX_ANCHOR_NOT_PHASE_ROW` if they are routed through `Impact`/`Duration`/`Cessation` scheduling instead of direct placed-object/model-emitter handling.
   - VFX palette resrefs emit `VFX_VFX_PALETTE_RESREF_NOT_VISUALEFFECTS_ROW` if they become row IDs or source-table labels.
   - Direct emitter MDLs on placed VFX objects emit `VFX_PLACEABLE_EMITTER_MODEL_DIRECT_NOT_PHASE_SCHEDULE` if used to synthesize an `AuroraVfxPhaseSchedule`.
   - `EffectVisualEffect` and hardcoded VFX constructors require row-ID provenance and emit `VFX_VISUALEFFECTS_ROW_ID_REQUIRED_FOR_EFFECT_CONSTRUCTOR` when only a placeable/source-list entry exists.
   - Preserve-only `vfxPayload` fields emit `VFX_PLACEABLE_VFX_PRESERVE_PAYLOAD_PREVIEW_ONLY` if frontend or backend treats them as canonical runtime state.
   - Processing graph `vfx_preset` nodes and catalog `vfxPreset` metadata stay resource-graph/catalog identities, not `AuroraVfxSourceRow` or `visualeffects.2da` identities. They may be attached as preview/dependency graph hints only after canonical source-row provenance is present; using them as row IDs, phase schedules, or effect-instance sources emits `VFX_PROCESSING_GRAPH_VFX_PRESET_NOT_VISUALEFFECTS_ROW`, `VFX_CURRENT_VFX_PRESET_RESOURCE_NODE_PREVIEW_ONLY`, or `VFX_CATALOG_VFXPRESET_METADATA_NOT_PHASE_SOURCE`.
   - `iprp_visualfx` table/suffix evidence emits `VFX_IPRP_VISUALFX_NOT_VISUALEFFECTS_ROW` if merged into `visualeffects.2da` phases.

7. Minimal renderer, staged.
   - Stage A: shared Aurora animation evaluation plus particle runtime state: common constructor defaults, source-node pointer, target-offset animated-track application, runtime transform cache, active/free lists, age/lifetime, spawn reset, previous position, velocity, rotation, and deterministic-ish frame/seed state.
   - Stage B: `Fountain` normal textured quads with evaluated `birthrate`, evaluated `lifeExp`, color/alpha/size interpolation, and no atlas yet.
   - Stage C: atlas playback using post-evaluation `xgrid`, `ygrid`, `frameStart`, `frameEnd`, source/evaluated `fps`, per-particle frame state, frame-step checkpoint, and `random` bit `0x20`.
   - Stage D: chunk MDL particle resolution and non-canonical preview adapter, with diagnostics if canonical chunk rendering is unavailable.
   - Stage E: `Explosion` plus `detonate` event timing and post-fire reset.
   - Stage F: `Single` with max-one-particle and loop/life behavior.
   - Stage G: `Normal`, local/world Z billboards, aligned modes, render-order sorting, and unknown-render diagnostics.
   - Stage H: Aurora render-state adapter plus `Punch-Through` vs mode-`2`/Lighten-candidate comparison against the real client.
   - Stage I: `Linked` and `Motion_Blur`, including segment topology and previous-position handling.
   - Stage J: P2P/Gravity/Bezier validation and non-canonical preview only after reference-node resolution.
   - Stage K: `Lightning` fourth update path with segment/timer/reference-target runtime, then compare against the real client.
   - Stage L: canonical chunk MDL particles if Stage D remains preview-only.
   - Stage M: MTR/TXI/custom shader parity: preserve texture sidecars, MTR slots/parameters/custom shaders, PLT profile gates, and shader-lane diagnostics before any MTR-driven visual approximation.
   - Stage N: EE `progfx.2da` typed preview adapters, starting with preserve/diagnostics only, then simple static glow/pulse families, and only later beams/MIRVs/node-attached VFX after effect-instance and retail validation are ready.

8. Blender integration policy.
   - Treat Blender/NeverBlender as authoring/reference UI only.
   - Do not use Blender particle simulation as runtime ground truth.
   - Do not use Blender or NeverBlender default particle values as Aurora runtime constructor defaults.
   - Build any future Blender adapter around separate `auroraRaw`, `auroraNormalized`, `blenderAuthoring`, and `blenderPreview` payload lanes.
   - Do not let Blender `ParticleSettings`, `ParticleSystem`, `PointCache`, F-Curve evaluation, or NeverBlender UI-only fields overwrite raw Aurora source rows or normalized Aurora runtime records.

## Aurora Retail Validation Harness Contract

Retail validation is not a substitute for Aurora decompilation. It is the way to close the gaps where decompilation gives branch structure or string evidence but not exact visual/output behavior.

1. Validation profiles:
   - Record client family: classic/Aurora, NWN:EE stable build, or NWN:EE dev build.
   - Record renderer configuration: lighting/shader quality, post-processing, gamma/brightness, resolution, camera mode, FOV, UI scale, pause state, and any debug-render toggles.
   - Record module state: module name, area tag, HAK order, override state, NWSync/patch state, and resource policy ID/version.
   - Record VFX source state: selected `visualeffects.2da`, optional `progfx.2da`, source layer winner, raw row, parsed row JSON, resolved model/texture/sound/material refs, and diagnostics.
   - A capture without this profile is not evidence. Emit `VFX_RETAIL_CAPTURE_PROFILE_MISSING`.

2. Retail command/test entry points:
   - Use `dm_visualeffect <row> <duration>` for rows that can play from a selected object/location. NWN Wiki documents that it targets a `visualeffects.2da` line and maps to `EffectVisualEffect`.
   - Do not use `dm_visualeffect` as the only beam/MIRV proof. The same source notes that VFX requiring a source object, such as MIRV-style effects, will not work through that simple command path.
   - Use a scripted test module for `EffectVisualEffect` and `EffectBeam` so object, location, duration, miss flag, scale, translate, rotate, source object, target object/location, and `BODY_NODE_*` context can all be controlled.
   - Use debug UI/options only after command availability is confirmed for the target build. Beamdog/SteamDB release notes verify debug UI support for `renderaab` and `rendertilepathnodes`; `renderemitter` remains a candidate/manual note unless confirmed in the exact client.
   - Any unverified command produces `VFX_RETAIL_DEBUG_COMMAND_UNVERIFIED`, not a failed VFX parser result.

3. Required fixture families:
   - `visualeffects.2da` row families: instant (`F`), duration (`D`), beam (`B`), persistent/permanent (`P`), rows with blank phase slots, rows with sounds, and rows with `ProgFX_*` refs.
   - MDL emitter families: Fountain textured, Fountain trail, Explosion with `detonate`, Single loop/non-loop, Lightning/P2P with child reference nodes, chunk particles, `Linked`, `Motion_Blur`, atlas/random frame playback, `Normal`, `Punch-Through`, and mode-`2`/Lighten-candidate blend.
   - `progfx.2da` families: static/glow-like rows, pulse rows, beam rows, MIRV rows, Type 12 node-attached rows, Type 8 delete/unload model, and Type 9 hardcoded chunk.
   - Resource resolver families: module-vs-HAK conflict, HAK order conflict, override conflict, missing texture, missing chunk model, TXI sidecar, MTR sidecar/custom shader, PLT texture with object-layer colours, TPC/DDS/TGA candidates.
   - Local repo fixture candidates: `backend/tmp_cot_fx01.mdl`, benchmark candidate `placeable_vfx_plc_alt`, and current HAK hints `lc_vfx.hak` / `cep3_vfx.hak`.

4. What must be captured:
   - Retail screenshot/video sequence with frame/time labels.
   - Our parser snapshot JSON for the same row/model/resource set.
   - Resolver trace showing candidate resources, source layers, winner, and lower-precedence rows/resources ignored.
   - Runtime observation notes: emitter active state, effect application path, attachment target/body node, and duration/miss/transform inputs.
   - For blend/depth/order uncertainty, capture GPU/render-state evidence if possible; otherwise keep exact `glBlendFunc`, depth-write, and sort behavior diagnostic.
   - If capture artifacts are missing, emit `VFX_RETAIL_CAPTURE_ARTIFACT_MISSING`.

5. Behaviors to close with retail comparison:
   - Exact `blend` mode equations and depth-write behavior for `Normal`, `Punch-Through`, and fallback/mode-`2` literals.
   - Exact distinction, if any, between `Normal` and fallback/mode-`2` non-punch equations, because the current C export shows the same visible state wrapper sequence for both.
   - `renderorder` sort priority, especially when transparent particles overlap chunk particles or placeable/model VFX.
   - Particle cap/overflow behavior and active/free list reuse visible consequences.
   - Collision/bounce/splat/walkmesh interactions.
   - Atlas integer step rounding/tie behavior, random start frame behavior, range direction retail parity, and frame-end inclusivity.
   - `Linked` segment topology and `Motion_Blur` previous-position stretching.
   - P2P/Gravity/Bezier/Lightning reference-node behavior.
   - Chunk model loading, transform, lighting/fog inheritance, and resource cleanup.
   - TXI/MTR/custom-shader influence on emitter particles versus ordinary model materials.
   - PLT visual-effect layer-colour inheritance from the object the effect is applied to.
   - EE effect transform handling for `EffectVisualEffect` and `EffectBeam`.
   - `OrientWithGround`, `OrientWithObject`, `InheritScale`, `BodyNode`, and phase sound scheduling behavior on object, location, beam, and duration applications.
   - `progfx.2da` Type 4/5/7/8/9/10/12 behavior before any canonical browser renderer claims.

6. Acceptance policy:
   - A renderer behavior becomes canonical only when Aurora/decomp evidence and retail observation agree, or when the difference is explicitly recorded as profile-specific behavior.
   - If decompilation and retail diverge, keep both facts and emit `VFX_RETAIL_DECOMP_MISMATCH`.
   - If resource precedence differs between project policy and retail, emit `VFX_RETAIL_RESOURCE_PRECEDENCE_CONFLICT` and do not hide the trace.
   - If effect context is missing for a beam/MIRV/source-dependent row, emit `VFX_RETAIL_EFFECT_CONTEXT_INCOMPLETE`.
   - If screenshots/videos exist but no frame-level comparison has been made, emit `VFX_RETAIL_SCREENSHOT_PARITY_UNVERIFIED`.
   - Store future binary capture artifacts outside this text report, then link them here by date/build/profile.

## Test Requirements

Backend tests to add before implementation:

1. Generic source-preserving 2DA parser.
   - `2DA V2.0` header is required/preserved and invalid headers emit `VFX_2DA_VERSION_HEADER_INVALID`
   - optional `DEFAULT:` value is preserved as table metadata and never silently substituted into raw VFX cells
   - `DEFAULT:` metadata is not substituted into raw cells, selected phase cells, or dependency edges, and misuse emits `VFX_2DA_DEFAULT_NOT_RAW_CELL`
   - leading blank lines before the header are tolerated, while blank text rows after the header are skipped without incrementing physical data row IDs
   - blank physical text rows never create empty VFX rows or shift downstream row IDs; row-shift behavior emits `VFX_2DA_BLANK_LINE_ROW_SHIFT_FORBIDDEN`
   - header lookup is column-name driven and order independent
   - the ignored/blank first header column is not treated as a typed data column
   - physical data row ID is preserved separately from first-column label
   - physical parsed data-row index is the canonical engine row ID for `visualeffects.2da`; using first-column tokens, constants, filenames, or compacted nonblank labels emits `VFX_VISUALEFFECTS_PHYSICAL_ROW_ID_REQUIRED` or `VFX_2DA_FIRST_COLUMN_NOT_ENGINE_ROW_ID`
   - first-column labels are recorded as provenance and emit `VFX_2DA_FIRST_COLUMN_NOT_ENGINE_ROW_ID` if a caller tries to use them as the runtime row ID
   - duplicate, missing, non-numeric, or non-sequential first-column labels produce diagnostics without renumbering physical rows
   - quoted cells survive tokenization without losing source value
   - `****` blank cells remain blank-cell state and are not normalized into resrefs
   - quoted blank/star cells preserve blank-cell state, while malformed star variants stay literal and can emit `VFX_2DA_MALFORMED_STAR_CELL_LITERAL`
   - missing required columns produce `VFX_2DA_REQUIRED_COLUMN_MISSING`
   - a missing column and a present column with `****` are distinguishable and can emit `VFX_2DA_MISSING_COLUMN_NOT_BLANK_CELL`
   - unknown columns preserve raw cells and provenance
   - source winner selection records selected layer and reports lower-precedence row availability without merging rows
   - VFX tests do not call the placeables-only `ModelName` parser path
   - current `aurora-web` placeable 2DA helpers are catalog/model-lookup parsers only: they search for `ModelName`, normalize model resrefs, filter blank/non-model rows, and drop raw cell/source-line provenance. VFX source parsing must reject those helpers through `VFX_2DA_PLACEABLES_MODELNAME_FILTER_NOT_VFX_PARSER`.
   - PoC `twoda_reader.py` is a useful comparison lookup helper, but its `get`/`get_int`/`get_float` methods substitute fallback/default values and its row objects do not preserve raw source-line/cell provenance. VFX source parsing must emit `VFX_POC_TWODA_LOOKUP_HELPER_NOT_SOURCE_PARSER` or `VFX_2DA_DEFAULT_NOT_RAW_CELL` if that helper is used to read raw phase cells, `****`, missing columns, or source-layer winners.
   - Current project parser refs: `backend/src/modules/catalog/adapters/outbound/blob/module-snapshot-template-catalog.repository.ts:1125-1193`
   - Current project parser refs: `backend/src/modules/runtime-settings/application/runtime-settings.application.service.ts:1364-1407`
   - PoC comparison source: `C:\Projects\nwn-last-city\Areas Generator 3d\Web Model Viewer\Common\twoda_reader.py:1-144`
   - Source for 2DA format, blank rows, first-column behavior, `DEFAULT:`, and `****`: https://nwn.wiki/spaces/NWN1/pages/38174875/2da%2BFiles
2. `visualeffects.2da` row parsing with `Type_FD`.
   - missing bootstrap/source table emits `VFX_2DA_BOOTSTRAP_TABLE_UNAVAILABLE`
   - bootstrap evidence records the neighboring table sequence and `visualeffects` owner slot `param_1[0x13]`
   - local decompilation proves only the `visualeffects` table bootstrap for this entry path; missing local `progfx`/`EffectVisualEffect`/`EffectBeam`/`BODY_NODE` strings emits `VFX_DECOMP_EFFECT_ENTRY_SYMBOLS_ABSENT` when those names are used as proof
   - `strings_2da.tsv` / `2da.csv` export membership is not table-registry proof; using those files to prove presence/absence of `visualeffects`, `progfx`, `vfx_persistent`, `iprp_visualfx`, or column schemas emits `VFX_DECOMP_STRINGS_2DA_EXPORT_NOT_TABLE_REGISTRY`, `VFX_DECOMP_2DA_CSV_NOT_SOURCE_TABLE_CONTENT`, `VFX_DECOMP_2DA_CSV_STRING_FILTER_NOT_SCHEMA_SOURCE`, `VFX_DECOMP_STRING_ABSENCE_NOT_TABLE_ABSENCE`, or `VFX_DECOMP_RESOURCE_STRING_REQUIRES_CALLSITE`
   - physical row ID vs first-column label mismatch
   - physical row ID, first-column label, NWScript constant name, and source file/profile are preserved separately
   - using a first-column label or `VFX_*` constant name as the physical engine row emits `VFX_VISUALEFFECTS_LABEL_NOT_ROW_ID`
   - row IDs above the selected profile's transport/storage limit emit `VFX_VISUALEFFECTS_ROW_ID_WORD_LIMIT`
   - out-of-profile row IDs emit `VFX_2DA_ROW_ID_OUT_OF_PROFILE_LIMIT`
   - client/server table ownership and transport-limit profile are recorded for VFX row IDs; missing profile evidence emits `VFX_VISUALEFFECTS_CLIENT_SERVER_PROFILE_REQUIRED`
   - row `999` is preserved as a special-profile/cow-cheat line and emits `VFX_VISUALEFFECTS_ROW_999_SPECIAL_CASE` if used as proof for ordinary custom row behavior
   - unknown `Type_FD` preservation
   - Aurora/NWN1 impact model refs, cessation model refs, sounds, fallback refs, and `ProgFX_*` phase refs remain separate
   - impact root-size slots `Imp_Root_S/M/L/H_Node` and cessation root-size slots `Ces_Root_S/M/L/H_Node` are preserved separately and emit `VFX_2DA_ROOT_SIZE_SLOT_PRESERVED`
   - root-size slots are alternative phase candidates selected by runtime target/object-size context; rendering all `S/M/L/H` slots together emits `VFX_2DA_ROOT_SIZE_SLOT_NOT_MULTI_SPAWN`
   - slot selection requires effect context, target class, attachment namespace, and size/root category; row-only selection emits `VFX_2DA_ROOT_SIZE_SLOT_SELECTION_CONTEXT_REQUIRED` or `VFX_PHASE_SLOT_SELECTED_BY_EFFECT_CONTEXT`
   - creature root-size slot selection records current appearance, `SIZECATEGORY`/`CREATURE_SIZE_*`, and polymorph/appearance-override provenance; missing target category emits `VFX_2DA_ROOT_SIZE_TARGET_CATEGORY_REQUIRED`, while non-polymorph-aware selection emits `VFX_2DA_ROOT_SIZE_TARGET_POLYMORPH_AWARE`
   - root-size slot selection based on MDL/GLB bounds, Three.js `Box3`/visible bounds, or Blender scale/dimensions emits `VFX_2DA_ROOT_SIZE_NOT_BBOX`, `VFX_2DA_ROOT_SIZE_NOT_BLENDER_SCALE`, `VFX_POC_BOUNDS_NOT_ROOT_SIZE_SELECTION`, or `VFX_PROJECT_GLB_BOUNDS_NOT_ROOT_SIZE_SELECTION`
   - non-creature and location-only root-size contexts remain unresolved unless retail/profile proof is present, emitting `VFX_2DA_ROOT_SIZE_NON_CREATURE_UNVERIFIED` or `VFX_2DA_ROOT_SIZE_LOCATION_ONLY_UNRESOLVED`
   - selected root-size phase-model cache keys include target identity, target kind, selected slot, current appearance/profile, `SIZECATEGORY`/`CREATURE_SIZE_*`, polymorph provenance, fallback diagnostic state, source layer, and profile; row/model-only keys emit `VFX_2DA_ROOT_SIZE_CACHE_KEY_TARGET_CONTEXT_REQUIRED`
   - `HeadCon`, `Impact`, and `Root_*` cells stay separate attachment namespaces and emit `VFX_2DA_PHASE_ATTACHMENT_NAMESPACE_REQUIRED` if collapsed
   - an empty unselected root-size slot is not an error, while an empty selected slot emits `VFX_PHASE_SLOT_EMPTY_SELECTED_DIAGNOSTIC`
   - no invented `S/M/L/H` fallback chain is applied; any fallback behavior remains diagnostic as `VFX_2DA_ROOT_SIZE_FALLBACK_UNVERIFIED` until retail/decomp proof exists
   - unknown/custom columns are preserved with provenance
   - column-schema assumptions record source/profile provenance and emit `VFX_2DA_COLUMN_SCHEMA_PROFILE_EVIDENCE_REQUIRED` when treated as decompilation proof
   - visualeffects column-name assumptions emit `VFX_2DA_COLUMN_NAMES_NOT_DECOMP_PROVEN` unless supported by selected source table/profile evidence
   - `Dur_*_Node` columns produce profile-mismatch diagnostics in Aurora/NWN1 profile while staying round-trippable, including `VFX_DUR_ROOT_NODE_PROFILE_MISMATCH` for invented/custom `Dur_Root_*_Node` columns
   - `DelayDurationFX` cells stay raw/profile-scoped and emit `VFX_2DA_DELAY_DURATION_FX_PROFILE_MISMATCH` in Aurora/NWN1 profile
   - `DelayDurationFX` emits `VFX_2DA_DELAY_DURATION_FX_NOT_PHASE_TIMER` if reused as `ProgFX_Duration`, `SoundDuration`, active-phase delay, `ApplyEffect*` requested duration, particle `lifeExp`, or browser preview cycle timing
   - repeated-row transform refresh tests remain retail-validation observations and emit `VFX_2DA_DELAY_DURATION_FX_NOT_REAPPLY_DELAY` if code reads the reapply-delay policy from a `DelayDurationFX` source cell
   - `.sef` references produce unsupported-profile diagnostics in Aurora/NWN1 profile while staying round-trippable
   - `ShakeType`, `ShakeDelay`, and `ShakeDuration` are preserved as auxiliary client-event fields and produce `VFX_2DA_SHAKE_CLIENT_EVENT_UNMAPPED` until the camera path is retail/decomp verified
   - selected-source fixtures assert `ShakeType=39`, `ShakeDelay=24`, and `ShakeDuration=28`, and preserve exemplar rows `22`, `30`, `286`, `287`, `356`, `644`, and `645`; count drift without profile provenance emits `VFX_2DA_SHAKE_SELECTED_ROW_SHAPE_PRESERVED`
   - nonblank `ShakeType` rows produce shake/bump client-event candidates regardless of label; limiting support to `VFX_FNF_SCREEN_SHAKE` / `VFX_FNF_SCREEN_BUMP` emits `VFX_2DA_SHAKE_NOT_SCREEN_CONSTANT_ONLY`
   - `ShakeType` raw cells are retained even when profile documentation maps `0/1/2`; guessed enum maps emit `VFX_2DA_SHAKE_TYPE_ENUM_PROFILE_REQUIRED`
   - `ShakeDelay` requires effect-application/phase timebase provenance and emits `VFX_2DA_SHAKE_DELAY_APPLICATION_TIME_REQUIRED` or `VFX_CLIENT_EVENT_DELAY_TIMEBASE_REQUIRED` if bound to Blender frames, MDL keyframes, render frames, or browser wall-clock time
   - `ShakeDuration` emits `VFX_2DA_SHAKE_DURATION_NOT_EFFECT_LIFETIME` when reused as particle `lifeExp`, preview cycle length, `ApplyEffect*` duration, sound duration, or row `Type_FD` duration
   - `SoundImpact=sff_screenbump` or `SoundImpact=sff_screenshake` does not by itself create a shake/bump client event; rows such as `644`/`645` with blank shake cells emit `VFX_2DA_SCREENBUMP_SOUND_NOT_SHAKETYPE` if converted from sound label alone
   - screen shake row constants remain selected-profile row evidence and emit `VFX_2DA_SHAKE_ROW_CONSTANT_PROFILE_ONLY` if treated as local decompilation proof
   - screen shake/bump rows produce `VFX_2DA_SHAKE_NOT_MDL_EMITTER` when a renderer attempts to model them as MDL emitters or attached phase models
   - local `bumpmaptexture`, `bumpyshinytexture`, and `bumpreplacementtexture` material/TXI/MTR strings emit `VFX_BUMP_TEXTURE_NOT_SCREEN_BUMP_EVENT` if used as evidence for screen-bump behavior
   - shake/bump rows create `AuroraVfxClientEventRequest` records only after effect-instance context is available; row-only client events emit `VFX_CLIENT_EVENT_EFFECT_INSTANCE_REQUIRED`
   - shake/bump request visibility/client scope stays profile-gated and emits `VFX_CLIENT_EVENT_VISIBILITY_SCOPE_PROFILE_REQUIRED` until retail/decomp capture proves local-player, party, area, or observer behavior
   - `ShakeType` client events never resolve to `MdlNodeCamera` and emit `VFX_CLIENT_EVENT_SHAKE_NOT_CAMERA_NODE` if a camera node is used as their runtime proof
   - MDL camera-node factory evidence emits `VFX_MDL_CAMERA_NODE_FACTORY_NOT_SHAKE_PATH` if used to claim the `visualeffects.2da` shake implementation path
   - Three.js `PerspectiveCamera`/`OrbitControls` preview cameras emit `VFX_THREE_ORBIT_CAMERA_NOT_SHAKE_RUNTIME` or `VFX_2DA_SHAKE_BROWSER_CAMERA_PREVIEW_ONLY` if used as canonical Aurora runtime behavior
   - shake fields keep `VFX_2DA_SHAKE_RETAIL_CAPTURE_REQUIRED` until a selected retail/decomp path proves the camera manipulation branch, visibility scope, and timing bridge
   - Type 4 `progfx.2da` rows produce client-light/perception requests and emit `VFX_PROGFX_TYPE4_REQUEST_CONTEXT_REQUIRED` until phase and effect-instance context are present
   - Type 4 programmed light requests do not resolve to MDL `node light`; doing so emits `VFX_PROGFX_TYPE4_NOT_MDL_LIGHT_NODE`
   - Type 4 programmed light requests do not become generic Three.js point lights without profile/retail validation and emit `VFX_CLIENT_LIGHT_NOT_GENERIC_POINT_LIGHT`

   - MDL light direct/key/bezier tracks for `color`, `radius`, `shadowradius`, `verticaldisplacement`, and `multiplier` are preserved with target-offset provenance; dropping offsets, flattening tracks, or losing the light-node target lane emits `VFX_MDL_LIGHT_TRACK_OFFSET_PROVENANCE_REQUIRED`, `VFX_MDL_LIGHT_COLOR_RADIUS_TRACK_PRESERVED`, or `VFX_MDL_LIGHT_SHADOW_RADIUS_TRACK_PRESERVED`
   - MDL light flags (`ambientonly`, `shadow`, `isdynamic`/`nDynamicType`, `affectdynamic`) stay on the light-node lane and emit `VFX_MDL_LIGHT_DYNAMIC_FLAGS_PRESERVED` if replaced by generic renderer-light defaults
   - light flare `texturenames`, `flaresizes`, `flarepositions`, `flarecolorshifts`, `flareradius`, and `generateflare` preserve raw list form and cardinality; counted/endlist form loss, mismatches, unresolved texture lanes, or promoted scalar assumptions emit `VFX_MDL_LIGHT_FLARE_LIST_FORM_PRESERVED`, `VFX_MDL_LIGHT_FLARE_LIST_CARDINALITY_REQUIRED`, `VFX_MDL_LIGHT_FLARE_TEXTURE_RESOLVE_REQUIRED`, or `VFX_MDL_LIGHT_FLARERADIUS_WRITE_UNVERIFIED`

   - `fadingLight` never becomes phase duration, `Type_FD`, particle `lifeExp`, or cessation timing and emits `VFX_MDL_LIGHT_FADING_NOT_PHASE_DURATION` when collapsed into those fields
   - area/tile light overrides, `lightcolor.2da`, and PoC `Tile_MainLight*`/`Tile_SrcLight*` metadata stay separate from MDL light-node payload and emit `VFX_MDL_LIGHT_AREA_TILE_LIGHT_SEPARATION_REQUIRED` or `VFX_MDL_LIGHT_TILE_OVERRIDE_CONTEXT_REQUIRED` if merged
   - EE lighting-engine, VFX-based-light fade, and debug light-range evidence is renderer-profile evidence; missing selected profile emits `VFX_MDL_LIGHT_EE_RENDERER_PROFILE_REQUIRED`
   - MDL light shadow flags and shadow-radius tracks do not become hidden mesh shadow-proxy filters and emit `VFX_MDL_LIGHT_SHADOW_NOT_SHADOW_PROXY_MESH` if mapped through PoC shadow-proxy logic

   - `classification effect` / `classification effects` fixtures remain model metadata and emit `VFX_MODEL_CLASSIFICATION_EFFECT_NOT_VFX_ROW` if converted into a `visualeffects.2da` row, `EffectVisualEffect` instance, `progfx.2da` request, or emitter-family selector
   - supermodel chains remain animation/model dependency edges and emit `VFX_MODEL_SUPERMODEL_NOT_EMITTER_SOURCE` if flattened into emitter source payload, Blender parentage, or texture/model cache keys without chain provenance
   - `setanimationscale` remains model animation metadata and emits `VFX_MODEL_ANIMATION_SCALE_NOT_TIMEBASE` if used as Blender FPS, scene frame conversion, effect duration, particle lifetime, or animation-event tick length
   - model propagation callbacks produce `AuroraMdlPropagationEvent` records and emit `VFX_MODEL_PROPAGATION_EVENT_RECORD_REQUIRED` if only a final visibility/tint/cull state is recorded

   - `propagaterender` emits `VFX_MODEL_PROPAGATERENDER_CALLBACK_NOT_VISIBILITY_FLAG` if mapped to `visibleByDefault`, Blender `hide_render`, Three.js `Object3D.visible`, or emitter render mode
   - `propagateviewvolume` emits `VFX_MODEL_PROPAGATEVIEWVOLUME_CALLBACK_NOT_CULLING` if mapped to particle active/free list draw gating, mesh frustum culling, or preview bounds filtering without propagation-event evidence
   - `diewithoutparent` emits `VFX_MODEL_DIEWITHOUTPARENT_CONTEXT_REQUIRED` unless parent/object lifecycle context is present; it never substitutes for phase duration, `Type_FD`, particle `lifeExp`, or a preview auto-dispose rule
   - PoC `visibleByDefault`, `render 0`, and `shadow_proxy` policies emit `VFX_POC_VISIBLEBYDEFAULT_NOT_AURORA_PROPAGATION`, `VFX_POC_RENDER_ZERO_POLICY_PREVIEW_ONLY`, or `VFX_POC_SHADOW_PROXY_NOT_MDL_LIGHT_SHADOW` if used as Aurora model-propagation or MDL light-shadow semantics
   - MDL `node camera` records stay model-node/preview metadata and emit `VFX_MDL_CAMERA_NODE_NOT_SHAKE_EVENT` if used as proof of visualeffects screen-shake behavior
   - `LowViolence` and `LowQuality` cells are preserved as source-row alternates and do not replace primary phase resources at parse time
   - low-setting fallback selection emits `VFX_2DA_LOW_SETTING_FALLBACK_RUNTIME_UNVERIFIED` until client setting and retail/decomp branch behavior are proven
   - low-setting fallback selection requires an explicit selected profile/runtime setting record and emits `VFX_2DA_LOW_SETTING_PROFILE_REQUIRED` when guessed from parser state alone
   - low-setting fallback cells are never treated as lower source-layer precedence and emit `VFX_2DA_LOW_SETTING_NOT_RESOLVER_PRECEDENCE` if they merge data from a lower-precedence `visualeffects.2da`
   - low-setting fallback targets preserve target-kind diagnostics (`rowRef`, `modelRef`, or `unknown`) and emit `VFX_2DA_LOW_FALLBACK_TARGET_KIND_UNVERIFIED` until the selected table profile proves the interpretation
   - missing `LowViolence`/`LowQuality` columns, present blank cells, literal `0`, and non-empty fallback tokens remain distinguishable; collapsing them emits `VFX_2DA_LOW_SETTING_BLANK_VS_MISSING_PRESERVED`
   - public docs that call a fallback a "VFX" or "vfx model" do not prove row-vs-model target kind; using that wording as canonical target-kind proof emits `VFX_2DA_LOW_FALLBACK_PUBLIC_DOC_AMBIGUOUS`
   - treating `LowQuality` as a direct MDL/model resref without selected-profile proof emits `VFX_2DA_LOW_FALLBACK_NOT_DIRECT_MODEL_RESREF_WITHOUT_PROFILE`
   - low-setting fallback chains require cycle protection and emit `VFX_2DA_LOW_FALLBACK_CHAIN_GUARD_REQUIRED` before any nested row schedule is built
   - Blender `display_percentage`, viewport display amount, viewport shading, and particle cache state emit `VFX_2DA_LOW_SETTING_NOT_BLENDER_DISPLAY_QUALITY` if used to choose Aurora `LowQuality` or `LowViolence`
   - PoC/image-generator `--quality`, `quality_scale`, bilinear filtering, panel size, crop, or hide-roofs flags emit `VFX_2DA_LOW_SETTING_NOT_POC_RENDER_QUALITY` if used as Aurora fallback selection
   - PoC web-runtime tuning constants such as `VFX_SIZE_SCALE`, `VFX_FORCE_SCALE`, `VFX_DENSITY_SCALE`, additive/normal/smoke alpha multipliers, particle-size clamps, and synthetic single-loop spin/pulse values emit `VFX_2DA_LOW_SETTING_NOT_POC_VFX_RUNTIME_TUNING` if used to select or prove `LowQuality`, `LowViolence`, fallback target kind, resource identity, or Aurora runtime profile
   - selected low-setting fallback requires an explicit profile decision/cache-key component and emits `VFX_2DA_LOW_SETTING_SELECTION_RECORD_REQUIRED` or `VFX_2DA_LOW_SETTING_CACHE_KEY_REQUIRED` when omitted
   - `OrientWithGround`, `OrientWithObject`, `InheritScale`, and `BodyNode`-style cells preserve raw source/header/profile data and do not rewrite MDL emitter `render` or Blender particle orientation settings
   - missing `OrientWithObject` column in old/profile variants is distinguishable from explicit blank/zero value and can emit `VFX_2DA_ORIENTWITHOBJECT_PATCH164_EXTERNAL` when patch-era provenance is needed
   - unverified row-orientation/scale behavior emits `VFX_2DA_ORIENTATION_FLAGS_RUNTIME_UNVERIFIED` until client branch or retail capture proves the transform policy
   - using row-orientation flags as emitter render-mode proof emits `VFX_2DA_ORIENTATION_FLAG_NOT_EMITTER_RENDER`
   - `SoundImpact`, `SoundDuration`, and cessation sound cells remain sound-resource/event fields separate from phase model refs, `ProgFX_*`, and MDL emitters
   - `SoundCessastion`/corrected cessation spelling variants preserve the physical header and emit `VFX_2DA_SOUND_CESSATION_SPELLING_VARIANT` when aliasing is applied
   - `visualeffects.2da` rows preserve the raw `SoundCessastion` source-header spelling and emit `VFX_VISUALEFFECTS_SOUNDCESSASTION_HEADER_PRESERVED` if export/DTO/debug output silently corrects it
   - corrected `SoundCessation` headers require source/profile evidence and emit `VFX_2DA_SOUND_CESSATION_ALIAS_SOURCE_REQUIRED` if accepted by typo-normalization alone
   - AOE `SoundCessation` stays in the `vfx_persistent.2da` lifecycle lane and emits `VFX_AOE_SOUNDCESSATION_NOT_VISUALEFFECTS_PHASE` if merged into normal `visualeffects.2da` phase sound scheduling
   - sound-only or missing-model rows do not synthesize invisible particle emitters; using sound cells as model refs emits `VFX_2DA_SOUND_PHASE_NOT_MODEL_RESOURCE`
   - `SoundDuration` scheduling requires effect-instance lifetime/application context and emits `VFX_2DA_SOUND_DURATION_INSTANCE_REQUIRED` when only the row is available
   - `SoundImpact`, `SoundDuration`, and `SoundCessastion` produce `AuroraVfxSoundEventRef`-style records with raw cell, physical header, normalized resref, requested resource class `sound`, source layer, phase, application mode, anchor context, and diagnostics
   - phase sound refs create `AuroraVfxAudioRuntimeRequest` records with WAV/sound resource edges and emit `VFX_AUDIO_RUNTIME_LANE_REQUIRED` or `VFX_AUDIO_WAVE_RESOURCE_EDGE_REQUIRED` if reduced to a particle/emitter or generic URL
   - audio requests require target/location anchor context and selected audio profile/settings; missing context emits `VFX_AUDIO_ANCHOR_OBJECT_LOCATION_REQUIRED` or `VFX_AUDIO_SETTINGS_PROFILE_REQUIRED`
   - `SoundImpact` is validated as an application/impact event and emits `VFX_2DA_SOUND_IMPACT_APPLICATION_EVENT` if scheduled from particle birth, emitter activation, atlas playback, or material/shader state
   - `SoundDuration` loop/start/stop behavior remains `VFX_2DA_SOUND_DURATION_LOOP_POLICY_UNVERIFIED` until a retail/decompilation fixture proves the exact scheduler
   - duration sound loop/stop behavior emits `VFX_AUDIO_DURATION_LOOP_POLICY_RUNTIME_UNVERIFIED` until the runtime scheduler is proven
   - `SoundCessastion`/`SoundCessation` is validated as a removal/cessation event and emits `VFX_2DA_SOUND_CESSATION_REMOVAL_EVENT` if attached to particle expiration or MDL animation end without effect-removal context
   - AOE `SoundImpact`/`SoundDuration`/`SoundCessation` columns remain in the AOE pseudo-object lane and emit a namespace diagnostic if merged with normal `visualeffects.2da` sounds
   - preview audio playback emits `VFX_AUDIO_PREVIEW_NON_CANONICAL` unless the schedule, anchor, resource, and lifetime behavior are fixture-proven for the selected profile
   - WebAudio/OpenAL-style preview playback emits `VFX_AUDIO_OPENAL_PREVIEW_NON_CANONICAL` if it is used as canonical runtime proof
   - client range replays for duration VFX stay profile/fixture-gated and emit `VFX_AUDIO_CLIENT_RANGE_REPLAY_PROFILE_GATED` until retail validation closes the behavior
   - missing WAV/sound resources emit `VFX_AUDIO_MISSING_WAVE_DOES_NOT_DROP_PHASE` and do not suppress model/progFX/phase records
   - PlaySound, sound objects, and soundsets stay comparison APIs/tables only; using them as phase sound proof emits `VFX_AUDIO_SOUND_OBJECT_NOT_VFX_PHASE` or `VFX_AUDIO_SOUNDSET_NOT_PHASE_SOUND`
   - current `aurora-web` sound module records and frontend `Audio` playback are accepted only as asset/preview helpers and emit `VFX_CURRENT_SOUND_MODULE_PREVIEW_ONLY` / `VFX_AUDIO_HTML_AUDIO_PREVIEW_NON_CANONICAL` when used as canonical VFX scheduler proof
   - PoC `asset=sound`, `#sound-preview`, and browser `HTMLAudioElement` playback emit `VFX_POC_SOUND_ASSET_MODE_NOT_PHASE_AUDIO` / `VFX_POC_SOUND_HTML_AUDIO_PREVIEW_ONLY` when treated as canonical `SoundImpact`/`SoundDuration`/`SoundCessastion` behavior
   - runtime-settings `sources.sound` and `lc_audio` HAK profile selection emit `VFX_RUNTIME_SETTINGS_SOUND_PROFILE_NOT_VFX_PHASE_SOURCE` when treated as a VFX phase source instead of an audio resolver profile
   - scene sound bindings such as `GI_sound_area`, `GI_sound_rndm`, `GI_sound_pos`, `soundpal`, `soundset`, and `soundtypes` emit `VFX_SOUND_AREA_BINDING_NOT_PHASE_SOUND` if they replace `SoundImpact`/`SoundDuration`/`SoundCessastion` provenance
   - VFX phase sound tests require effect-instance context, phase source field, application mode, and anchor context; missing effect context emits `VFX_AUDIO_EFFECT_INSTANCE_CONTEXT_REQUIRED`
   - frontend `once`/`repeat`/`loop`, interval, random position, and simple attenuation policies emit `VFX_AUDIO_PREVIEW_INTERVAL_NOT_DURATION_POLICY` if they replace Aurora `SoundDuration` lifetime/loop/replay behavior
   - converting a VFX phase sound into a persistent scene sound object emits `VFX_VFX_PHASE_SOUND_NOT_SCENE_SOUND_OBJECT`
   - empty phase slot diagnostics are phase-aware, not blanket failures
   - model and sound resolution diagnostics are separate
   - a parsed row alone produces source facts and emits `VFX_PHASE_SOURCE_ROW_NOT_RUNTIME_SCHEDULE` if used as a runtime schedule
   - `AuroraVfxPhaseSchedule` construction requires constructed effect kind, application mode, duration type, requested duration, row `Type_FD`, miss flag, target kind/usability, phase, and phase source refs
   - schedule construction emits `VFX_PHASE_SCHEDULE_RECORD_REQUIRED` unless it produces typed phase records instead of a loose merged resource list
   - schedule output contains separate `apply`, `active`, and `remove` records; collapsing them emits `VFX_PHASE_APPLY_ACTIVE_REMOVE_SPLIT_REQUIRED`
   - model refs, `AuroraProgrammedFxRuntimeRequest` refs, and `AuroraVfxSoundEventRef` refs remain separate lanes; merging them emits `VFX_PHASE_MODEL_SOUND_PROGFX_LANE_COLLAPSED`
   - `ApplyEffectAtLocation` normal VFX paths remain event-style unless an explicit AOE/summon/swarm/persistent effect kind is present
   - `ApplyEffectToObject` instant paths remain event-style and do not become persistent scene children
   - `Type_FD = F` and `Type_FD = P` with temporary/permanent object application emit `VFX_PHASE_DURATION_TYPEFD_UNSUPPORTED` or an equivalent duration-coercion diagnostic
   - `Type_FD = D` and `Type_FD = B` may build duration schedules only when target object usability and effect context are present
   - duration behavior cannot be inferred from row `Type_FD` alone; row-only duration attempts emit `VFX_PHASE_DURATION_NOT_ROW_ONLY`
   - miss-flagged duration rows emit `VFX_PHASE_MISS_FLAG_FORCES_EVENT_STYLE` or an equivalent unreliable-duration diagnostic
   - duration schedules preserve separate impact/duration/cessation model, sound, and `ProgFX_*` refs
   - cessation/remove phase records do not fire during source parse, resource preload, or instant-only preview; doing so emits `VFX_PHASE_CESSATION_NOT_PRELOAD`
   - each phase event payload preserves typed request data and source field path; untyped payloads emit `VFX_PHASE_TYPED_EVENT_REQUEST_REQUIRED`
   - cache keys differ by phase, source field path, application mode, target/anchor, transform tuple, beam context, miss flag, and low-setting profile; insufficient keys emit `VFX_PHASE_CACHE_KEY_CONTEXT_REQUIRED`
   - every phase record exposes `canonicalStatus`; missing status emits `VFX_PHASE_STATUS_REQUIRED`
