   - missing `chunkName` MDL/model resources emit `VFX_CHUNK_MODEL_MISSING` and `VFX_CHUNK_MISSING_MODEL_NO_TEXTURE_FALLBACK`; they do not fall back to emitter `texture` as canonical behavior
   - if both `texture` and `chunkName` are present, `chunkName` chooses the chunk lane while the raw texture token remains preserved for round-trip/source diffing
   - sidecar TXI directives are preserved raw, and unsupported directives remain round-trippable
   - TXI/MTR/SHD sidecars preserve their owning texture/material/shader edge and emit `VFX_RESOURCE_SIDE_CAR_OWNER_REQUIRED` if detached from owner context
   - runtime-settings `texture-index/v1` results are reclassified before VFX use; `txi`, `mtr`, `plt`, and shader refs never enter canonical VFX as generic image blobs and emit `VFX_TEXTURE_INDEX_RESOURCE_KIND_REQUIRED`, `VFX_TEXTURE_INDEX_SIDECAR_NOT_IMAGE_BLOB`, or `VFX_TEXTURE_INDEX_MATERIAL_NOT_IMAGE_BLOB` when flattened
   - VFX dependency edges never use only `textureId`/delivery URL; missing requested resource class, resource type, owner field path, or canonical use emits `VFX_TEXTURE_INDEX_TEXTURE_URL_NOT_RESOURCE_EDGE`
   - TXI atlas/animation directives never override emitter-side `xgrid/ygrid/frameStart/frameEnd/fps/random`
   - TXI sampler-style directives such as clamp/filter/mipmap/gamma stay separate from Three.js `Texture.wrapS`, `wrapT`, `colorSpace`, and `flipY`, and emit `VFX_TXI_SAMPLER_DIRECTIVE_REQUIRED` when canonical sampler state is requested without TXI/profile proof
   - TXI `gamma` remains a texture-side directive and emits `VFX_TXI_GAMMA_NOT_BLENDER_COLORSPACE` if replaced by Blender `Image.colorspace_settings`, scene color management, Three.js `texture.colorSpace`, or screenshot display transform
   - TXI `alphamean` remains texture/shader sidecar evidence and emits `VFX_TXI_ALPHAMEAN_NOT_PARTICLE_ALPHA` if it rewrites `alphaStart`, `alphaMid`, `alphaEnd`, mesh `alpha`, `transparencyhint`, material `transparency`, or generic opacity
   - Blender `Image.alpha_mode` and Image Texture Alpha-output premultiply behavior are preview decode/material facts and emit `VFX_BLENDER_IMAGE_ALPHA_MODE_PREVIEW_ONLY`, `VFX_BLENDER_IMAGE_PREMULTIPLY_NOT_PARTICLE_ALPHA`, or `VFX_BLENDER_IMAGE_ALPHA_OUTPUT_NOT_SOURCE_ALPHA` if mapped to Aurora source fields
   - Blender `CHANNEL_PACKED` alpha emits `VFX_BLENDER_CHANNEL_PACKED_ALPHA_NOT_OPACITY` if treated as particle opacity, texture cutout, `alphamean`, or material transparency without source/profile proof
   - Blender `Image.colorspace_settings`, `use_view_as_render`, display/view transforms, exposure, and scene gamma emit `VFX_BLENDER_IMAGE_COLORSPACE_PREVIEW_ONLY`, `VFX_BLENDER_VIEW_AS_RENDER_NOT_AURORA_GAMMA`, or `VFX_BLENDER_COLOR_MANAGEMENT_NOT_SHADER_PROFILE` if used as Aurora TXI `gamma`, shader `GAMMA_CORRECTION`, emitter `colorStart/Mid/End`, mesh material color, or tint source
   - shader `GAMMA_CORRECTION` is represented as renderer-profile state and emits `VFX_SHADER_GAMMA_CORRECTION_PROFILE_REQUIRED` if a browser adapter guesses it from Blender/Three color-space settings
   - local texture-controller class names are preserved as evidence and emit `VFX_TEXTURE_CONTROLLER_CLASS_EVIDENCE_PRESERVED` when present
   - texture-controller class names require a recovered runtime owner/call-site before canonical use and emit `VFX_TEXTURE_CONTROLLER_RUNTIME_CALLSITE_REQUIRED` when used as behavior proof
   - texture-controller evidence does not override emitter atlas fields and emits `VFX_TEXTURE_CONTROLLER_NOT_EMITTER_ATLAS` if used to drive `frameStart/frameEnd/fps/random`
   - texture-controller evidence does not become TXI directives and emits `VFX_TEXTURE_CONTROLLER_NOT_TXI_DIRECTIVE` if used to fill `filerange`, sampler, or alpha directives
   - texture-controller evidence does not become MTR/custom shader behavior and emits `VFX_TEXTURE_CONTROLLER_NOT_MTR_SHADER` if used as a material program source
   - Three.js `Texture.colorSpace` and `flipY` values from preview loaders emit `VFX_TEXTURE_COLORSPACE_PROFILE_UNVERIFIED` or `VFX_TEXTURE_FLIPY_PROFILE_UNVERIFIED` if used as Aurora profile truth
   - TPC decode requirements are diagnosed separately from missing resource diagnostics
   - PLT texture refs are profile-gated and preserve unresolved object-layer colour source
   - MTR referenced by `materialname` or `bitmap` preserves texture slots, custom shaders, renderhint, and parameters
   - unresolved MTR `texture0..texture10` slots produce slot-specific diagnostics
   - custom MTR shaders are preserved/profile-gated as material-program rebind candidates and do not replace emitter blend, topology, or particle-update facts
   - VFX-resolved MDL meshes produce an `AuroraMdlMeshMaterialLane` record and emit `VFX_MDL_MESH_NODE_MATERIAL_LANE_REQUIRED` if mesh/material fields are reduced to particle material state
   - mesh `texture0..2`, `bitmap`, and MTR `materialname` remain separate owner edges and emit `VFX_MDL_MESH_TEXTURE_SLOTS_NOT_EMITTER_TEXTURE`, `VFX_MDL_MESH_BITMAP_ALIAS_PRESERVED`, or `VFX_MDL_MESH_MATERIALNAME_RESOURCE_EDGE` if collapsed into emitter `texture`, `chunkName`, or one generic texture key
   - mesh `render` and `renderhint` stay mesh/material fields and emit `VFX_MDL_MESH_RENDER_FLAG_NOT_EMITTER_RENDER` or `VFX_MDL_MESH_RENDERHINT_MATERIAL_LANE` if used as emitter `render` mode, particle billboarding, or renderer-family selector
   - mesh animated `alpha` and `selfillumcolor` direct/key/bezier tracks survive import/export and emit `VFX_MDL_MESH_ALPHA_TRACK_NOT_PARTICLE_ALPHA` or `VFX_MDL_MESH_SELFILLUM_TRACK_PROFILE_GATED` if converted to particle `alphaStart/alphaEnd`, particle tint, MDL light color, or GLB unlit output
   - mesh `rotatetexture` stays mesh/tile UV metadata and emits `VFX_MDL_MESH_ROTATETEXTURE_NOT_EMITTER_ATLAS` if used to rotate emitter quads, atlas cells, `frameStart`/`frameEnd`, `random`, or source emitter texture state
   - Blender texture-node rotation, UV transforms, or material preview rotation emit `VFX_BLENDER_TEXTURE_ROTATION_PREVIEW_ONLY` when used as proof for Aurora mesh `rotatetexture`
   - mesh `transparencyhint` and `tilefade` are preserved as source metadata and emit `VFX_MDL_MESH_TRANSPARENCYHINT_PRESERVED` or `VFX_MDL_MESH_TILEFADE_PREVIEW_POLICY_ONLY` when replaced by Blender `Alpha Clip`, Three `alphaTest`, PoC helper culling, or `visibleByDefault`
   - PoC `tilefade_gt_1` suspicious-mesh culling emits `VFX_POC_TILEFADE_CULLING_NOT_VFX_MESH_SOURCE` if it drops, hides, or rewrites VFX-spawned MDL mesh source records
   - PoC black-key transparency heuristics emit `VFX_POC_BLACK_KEY_TRANSPARENCY_NOT_TRANSPARENCYHINT_RUNTIME` if `black_pixel_ratio`, alpha-channel metadata, or alpha cutoff is treated as Aurora `transparencyhint` runtime behavior
   - particle shader profile define values are recorded before shader cache key or preview program selection
   - missing `.shd` resources and shader compile failures remain diagnostics instead of silently substituting a generic material
   - texture-unit binding uniforms and `texture%dBound`-style flags are represented separately from MTR texture slots
   - PLT scheme uniform requirements are recorded when PLT/profile-gated texture paths are present
   - `particleSoftness` is represented as particle-shader float slot `0` with a candidate uniform name until binding is proven
   - `sample_framebuffer` and `volumetric` stay material-lane diagnostics until runtime mapping is proven
   - VFX-spawned model resources are routed through a mesh/material/fog lane and emit `VFX_SPAWNED_MODEL_MESH_LANE_REQUIRED` if preview code tries to satisfy them with textured-particle quads
   - spawned-model fog and self-illum behavior is profile-gated and emits `VFX_SPAWNED_MODEL_FOG_PROFILE_GATED` / `VFX_SPAWNED_MODEL_SELFILLUM_PROFILE_GATED` until retail capture confirms selected-profile behavior
   - Blender `blend_method`, `surface_render_method`, `alpha_threshold`, and EEVEE alpha-mode choices are recorded only as preview-adapter output and emit `VFX_BLENDER_ALPHA_MODE_PREVIEW_ONLY` if exported as Aurora source

   - GLB `KHR_materials_unlit` material output is preview/export scaffolding and emits `VFX_GLB_UNLIT_MATERIAL_PREVIEW_ONLY` if used as canonical VFX material proof
   - current GLB `emitter_proxy` is flagged non-canonical when used for VFX preview
9. Texture atlas validation:
   - zero `xgrid`/`ygrid` normalize to one at runtime
   - raw source `xgrid/ygrid` zero or missing state is preserved separately from renderer-effective grid `1`
   - single-cell atlas state writes full-texture UVs and does not enter atlas frame-cell math
   - V coordinates use Aurora's top-down row calculation before writing the six vertex rows
   - `xgrid * ygrid` frame capacity is recorded without clamping raw fields away
   - direct, key, and bezier-key variants of `frameStart`, `frameEnd`, and `fps` survive parser preservation
   - token matching is case-insensitive for recovered local parser branches, so `Blend`, `spawnType`, `framestart`, and `frameend` match their canonical branches while preserving physical token spelling
   - case-insensitive branch matching does not admit unrelated helper/alias tokens such as `*_sel`, `p2p_type`, or `lightningSubDiv`
   - direct hidden-token branches such as `Drag`/direct `drag` require recovered direct-token provenance and do not become `dragkey`
   - direct/key/bezierkey `fps` variants preserve Aurora target offset `0x80` and emit `VFX_ATLAS_FPS_DIRECT_KEY_BEZIER_SAME_OFFSET_REQUIRED` if split into unrelated normalized fields
   - direct `fps` parser path accepts the unlabeled `DAT_00cc7914` token family as raw provenance
   - direct `fps` parser provenance emits `VFX_ATLAS_FPS_DIRECT_TOKEN_HIDDEN_PRESERVE_REQUIRED` if only `fpskey`/`fpsbezierkey` are retained
   - `deadspace` raw/provenance and parsed-float candidate survive import/export even when runtime use is unresolved
   - `deadspace` is represented as a hidden-target parsed-float candidate with no visible parse-helper destination, not as an animated target-offset family or writable source-emitter slot
   - `deadspace` public view-direction/aligned-particle description is retained as external authoring evidence, not runtime math
   - `deadspace` does not alter UVs, material offsets, atlas repeat, or frame-cell selection in canonical renderer tests until a deeper Aurora proof exists
   - `deadspace` does not become collision radius, arbitrary spawn culling, a preview rejection loop, Blender billboard alignment, texture crop, alpha fade, or `twosidedtex` behavior without recovered runtime evidence
   - `render Aligned_to_Particle_Dir` + camera-direction fixtures record `VFX_DEADSPACE_RETAIL_FIXTURE_REQUIRED` until the local branch or retail capture proves exact behavior
   - `random` playback maps to source flag bit `0x20`
   - per-particle frame slot and frame timer/checkpoint slot are initialized/reset before activation
   - sequential playback increments and decrements across `frameStart/frameEnd` ranges
   - reversed `frameStart > frameEnd` ranges remain reversed and emit `VFX_ATLAS_FRAME_RANGE_NOT_SORTED` if normalized into an ascending window before playback
   - atlas playback uses the per-particle checkpoint slot and emits `VFX_ATLAS_CHECKPOINT_PLAYBACK_REQUIRED` if replaced by stateless `floor(age * fps)` math
   - PoC-style `end < start` window swapping emits `VFX_POC_ATLAS_FRAME_WINDOW_SWAP_PREVIEW_ONLY`
   - per-particle UVs are written into the six vertex rows, not shared material state
   - Blender Image Texture sequence/movie controls (`Frames`, `Start Frame`, `Offset`, `Cyclic`, `Auto Refresh`) emit `VFX_BLENDER_IMAGE_TEXTURE_FRAME_NOT_PARTICLE_FRAME` if used instead of Aurora per-particle frame/checkpoint playback
   - Blender `Image.source` values `SEQUENCE`/`MOVIE` emit `VFX_BLENDER_IMAGE_SEQUENCE_NOT_ATLAS` if used to synthesize Aurora `xgrid`, `ygrid`, `frameStart`, `frameEnd`, `fps`, or `random`
   - Blender `Image.source = TILED` / UDIM tiles emit `VFX_BLENDER_UDIM_TILED_NOT_ATLAS_GRID` if converted to Aurora atlas grid cells
   - Blender Image Texture extension modes (`Repeat`, `Extend`, `Clip`, `Mirror`) emit `VFX_BLENDER_TEXTURE_EXTENSION_NOT_ATLAS_UV` if used to replace Aurora top-down atlas UV generation
   - missing texture on a textured emitter emits `VFX_TEXTURE_RESOURCE_MISSING_DIAGNOSTIC` without dropping source emitter fields
   - `texture NULL` with empty `chunkName` is preserved as explicit no-texture source state and emits `VFX_TEXTURE_NULL_NO_CHUNK_NO_TEXTURED_DRAW`
10. Chunk particle validation:
   - `chunkName` resolves through model-resource precedence
   - `chunkName` dependency edges record requested resource class `MDL/model`, source field path `emitter.chunkName`, candidate trace, selected source layer, and resolved runtime model reference when available
   - `chunkName` resolution emits `VFX_CHUNK_RESOLVER_NOT_TEXTURE_LOADER` if routed through texture/TXI/MTR lookup instead of model/MDL lookup
   - imported source emitters preserve the fixed `chunkName` buffer/provenance equivalent to Aurora source offset `+0x128` and emit `VFX_CHUNKNAME_SOURCE_BUFFER_10H_REQUIRED` if normalized as an arbitrary UI string before raw preservation
   - chunk-lane selection is gated by the non-empty first byte of the source `chunkName` buffer and emits `VFX_CHUNKNAME_FIRST_BYTE_LANE_GATE_REQUIRED` if driven by Blender `particletype`, a texture token, or a generic boolean
   - missing/empty `chunkName`, non-empty `chunkName`, missing `texture`, and `texture NULL` remain separate states and emit `VFX_CHUNKNAME_TEXTURE_NULL_STATE_SEPARATE` if collapsed
   - non-empty source `chunkName` buffer selects chunk lane; `texture NULL` alone does not
   - `chunkName` with `texture NULL` remains valid
   - `chunkName` overrides texture payload when both are present
   - raw `texture` remains preserved when `chunkName` overrides the runtime lane
   - chunk particle allocation uses the base-particle reset/init path before switching to chunk draw payload
   - chunk particle allocation installs a chunk vtable and emits `VFX_CHUNK_PARTICLE_VTABLE_REQUIRED` if it only toggles a source flag
   - canonical chunk particles carry a model/runtime pointer equivalent to Aurora `particle + 0x70` and emit `VFX_CHUNK_PARTICLE_MODEL_POINTER_SLOT70_REQUIRED` if only a shared model name or shared batch exists
   - resolved chunk model instances run initialization/reference hooks before rendering and emit `VFX_CHUNK_MODEL_RUNTIME_INIT_REQUIRED` if the resource is attached without runtime init provenance
   - expired/recycled chunk particles release or clear their model-resource pointer
   - chunk reuse emits `VFX_CHUNK_REUSE_RELEASE_BEFORE_RESET` if a reused particle accepts a new `chunkName` payload before the previous model slot has release/clear evidence
   - reused chunk particles clear stale model refs before accepting a new resolved model payload
   - canonical chunk renderer preserves per-particle model transform, evaluated size/scale, particle rotation, age/lifetime gates, and active/free-list ownership
   - chunk draw/update emits `VFX_CHUNK_RENDER_USES_MODEL_VTABLE` if rendering is satisfied by the textured quad vertex buffer, a white billboard, or a raw shared `InstancedMesh` with no per-particle Aurora model payload
   - chunk emitters do not apply `xgrid/ygrid/frameStart/frameEnd/fps/random` as texture-atlas playback unless retail evidence proves such behavior
   - chunk `sizeStart/sizeEnd` tests mark exact axis/uniform scaling as `VFX_CHUNK_SIZE_SCALE_PROFILE_UNVERIFIED` until fixture-validated
   - chunk `render`/`blend` source literals are preserved but do not make the textured shader-buffer lane canonical for chunk particles
   - missing chunk model produces diagnostics without dropping raw emitter
   - textured-quad renderer is not marked canonical for chunk emitters
   - white billboard output for non-empty `chunkName` emits `VFX_POC_CHUNK_WHITE_QUAD_PREVIEW_ONLY` and cannot satisfy canonical chunk tests
   - placeholder cube/box output emits `VFX_CHUNK_PLACEHOLDER_MODEL_PREVIEW_ONLY` unless explicitly requested as a debug visualization
   - Three.js `InstancedMesh` chunk batches emit `VFX_CHUNK_INSTANCED_MESH_ADAPTER_REQUIRES_AURORA_INSTANCE` until backed by per-particle Aurora chunk instances
   - chunk model meshes preserve their own MDL mesh/material lane and emit `VFX_CHUNK_MESH_MATERIAL_LANE_REQUIRED` if collapsed into emitter texture/blend/tint state
   - chunk resource ownership and release/clear assertions emit `VFX_CHUNK_RESOURCE_LIFECYCLE_NOT_BATCHED_AWAY` if a shared batch hides per-particle model pointer lifecycle
11. Runtime lifecycle tests:
   - expired particles move from active list to free list
   - active/free list storage preserves count/capacity semantics and active removal shifts later entries
   - active/free list append grows capacity from empty to `0x10`, then doubles when count reaches capacity
   - active/free list capacity is not treated as a canonical particle-count cap
   - no fixed `maxParticles`/density clamp is introduced for Fountain or Explosion without retail/decompilation evidence
   - render vertex-buffer capacity grows independently to fit `drawParticleCount * 6`
   - `Single` max-one-active and Lightning exact-count reconciliation remain family-specific rules, not global particle caps
   - external `500cm x 500cm` emitter-area guidance is recorded as authoring evidence and never applied as active-particle-count capping
   - `bboxMin`/`bboxMax` or debug AABB output do not become canonical emitter culling until the runtime branch or retail capture proves the policy
   - free-list particles are reused before new particle allocation
   - reused particles run the reset/init path before becoming active again
   - `xsize/ysize` direct/key/bezier-key values evaluate before particle reset uses spawn rectangle sampling
   - point emitters with zero evaluated area copy emitter origin exactly
   - point-emitter fixtures emit `VFX_EMITTER_SPAWN_RECTANGLE_POINT_ORIGIN_REQUIRED` if zero area still consumes random offsets
   - below-threshold dimensions preserve Aurora axis-gate diagnostics instead of becoming a continuous random rectangle

   - Blender Particle System `Emit From`/distribution settings emit `VFX_BLENDER_EMISSION_DISTRIBUTION_AUTHORING_ONLY` and never satisfy Aurora `spawntype`/spawn-rectangle runtime sampling by themselves
   - no-spread/no-rand velocity fixture verifies final particle velocity equals the orientation-derived direction vector multiplied by evaluated `velocity` in slots `+0x50/+0x54/+0x58`
   - randvel fixture records the inspected `0.01` gate and signed random speed term, emitting `VFX_EMITTER_RANDVEL_GATE_001_REQUIRED`, `VFX_EMITTER_RANDVEL_SIGNED_SPEED_TERM_REQUIRED`, and `VFX_EMITTER_RANDVEL_RANDOM_TERM_DIAGNOSTIC` until deterministic retail capture pins the RNG envelope
   - PoC positive-only `randvel` jitter and speed clamp emit `VFX_POC_RANDVEL_UNSIGNED_JITTER_PREVIEW_ONLY` unless the fixture is explicitly a preview comparison

   - moving-emitter `inheritvel` fixture verifies inherited-motion state is written to `particle +0x18/+0x1c/+0x20/+0x24`, not just normal velocity slots
   - moving-emitter `inheritvel` fixture verifies active update applies inherited-motion displacement and decays inherited magnitude after reset

   - parented-emitter fixture verifies MDL `parent` and base-node `position`/`orientation`/`scale` tracks are evaluated as source model-node context, not as VFX attachment target rewrites
   - `inheritcolor` fixture verifies model-node color inheritance provenance is not merged into emitter tint, particle color interpolation, light color, PLT, or material self-illumination lanes

   - `bounce` reflects velocity by contact normal and scales the result by `bounce_co`
   - `bounce` does nothing unless the parsed source bit is set and the runtime collision query reports contact
   - collision creates `AuroraParticleCollisionQuery` only after runtime particle state, predicted position, evaluated `bounce_co`, source flag word, and scene/area collision profile are available
   - collision fixtures preserve a per-emitter query helper identity/init argument trace and emit `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_QUERY_OBJECT_PER_EMITTER_REQUIRED` or `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_CACHE_QUERY_HELPER_REQUIRED` if helper state is flattened or omitted
   - each bounce query resets result/status/normal/list state before contact testing and emits `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_QUERY_RESET_REQUIRED` or `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_QUERY_STALE_HIT_FORBIDDEN` if stale hits or normals can survive between particles
   - contact normals preserve query slot provenance `+0x54/+0x58/+0x5c` and emit `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_QUERY_NORMAL_SLOT_REQUIRED` if normal data is accepted without slot evidence
   - collision query attempts without those inputs emit `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_REQUEST_REQUIRED`, `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_CONTEXT_REQUIRED`, or `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_SERVICE_PROFILE_GATED`
   - collision results preserve hit/no-hit/unsupported status, contact normal, reflected velocity, post-nudge position, settled decision, and landed flag write intent
   - missing contact normals or post-contact position nudge emit `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_CONTACT_NORMAL_REQUIRED` or `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_POSITION_NUDGE_REQUIRED`
   - texture and chunk particles keep separate collision lanes and emit `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_TEXTURE_CHUNK_LANE_SPLIT_REQUIRED` if chunk-specific model-list or extent behavior is applied to texture particles or dropped from chunk particles
   - chunk collision fixtures preserve the per-particle model pointer/list entry and emit `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_CHUNK_MODEL_LIST_REQUIRED` when the helper list at `query +0x10` is not represented
   - chunk collision fixtures preserve the size-start/evaluated-size extent candidate in the test endpoint and post-hit normal nudge, emitting `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_CHUNK_SIZE_EXTENT_REQUIRED` or `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_CHUNK_POST_HIT_NUDGE_REQUIRED` if those terms are omitted
   - the global collision vtable call remains profile-gated and emits `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_SERVICE_VTABLE_PROFILE_GATED` if a renderer claims canonical service parity without mapping or retail-capturing that call
   - generic Three.js raycast collision is accepted only as preview/debug and emits `VFX_PARTICLE_PREVIEW_RAYCAST_NON_CANONICAL`
   - Blender deflector settings and current frontend collision overlays are accepted only as authoring/debug evidence and emit `VFX_BLENDER_COLLISION_DEFLECTOR_NOT_AURORA_QUERY`, `VFX_BLENDER_COLLISION_CACHE_NOT_AURORA_RUNTIME`, or `VFX_FRONTEND_COLLISION_OVERLAY_NOT_VFX_COLLISION` when promoted to runtime collision proof
   - collision fixtures may preserve optional `AuroraParticleCollisionSurfaceContext`, but it is evidence-graded and emits `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_SURFACE_CONTEXT_PROFILE_GATED` if mesh kind, surface material row, source file, or mapped collision profile provenance is missing
   - `surfacemat.2da` rows and `Walk`/`WalkCheck` values can annotate a candidate hit but do not decide canonical bounce inclusion; fixtures emit `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_SURFACEMAT_NOT_SERVICE_PROOF` or `VFX_PARTICLE_COLLISION_WALKCHECK_NOT_BOUNCE_FILTER` if those values are used as the collision-service policy
   - PoC walkable-mask generation, `walkSurfacePolicy`, walk-hit selection, spawn placement, hidden AABB filtering, and camera collision are accepted only as area/debug tooling and emit `VFX_POC_WALK_SURFACE_NOT_VFX_COLLISION` when used to satisfy `bounce`, `splat`, landed-flag, or particle `threshold` behavior
   - `bounce_co` direct/key/bezier parser variants target offset `0x5c`
   - direct, key, and bezier-key variants of `bounce_co` survive parser preservation
   - post-bounce settled detection uses the Aurora speed-squared threshold `< 0.5`
   - particle reuse clears `particle + 0x68` before activation
   - particle reuse resets previous position slots `particle + 0x5c/0x60/0x64` from the new current position
   - settled/stopped particles preserve the per-particle landed flag required by `splat`
   - `splat` with a landed particle uses the render-state/end-size behavior instead of normal size interpolation
   - `splat` without the landed flag does not create a decal or force end-size handling
   - `splat` never emits decal/mesh-on-walkmesh output in canonical mode and emits `VFX_PARTICLE_SPLAT_NOT_DECAL` if a renderer treats it as one
   - landed `splat` render tests require the end-size gate and emit `VFX_PARTICLE_SPLAT_END_SIZE_GATE_REQUIRED` if normal interpolation continues
   - `threshold` cannot be used as collision radius or rest distance and emits `VFX_PARTICLE_THRESHOLD_NOT_COLLISION_RADIUS` in collision fixtures
   - P2P/gravity `threshold` expires particles when the target-distance gate is crossed
   - particle rotation advances by `particleRot * delta` and wraps
   - `Explosion` uses a detonate latch plus one-shot guard and resets the latch after firing
   - `Single` source `loop` parses into source emitter offset `+0x13c` and defaults to zero in the source constructor
   - `Single` parser provenance preserves the anonymous `DAT_00cc6ff0`/`DAT_00cc6ff5` `loop` branch and emits `VFX_SINGLE_LOOP_HIDDEN_TOKEN_PROVENANCE_REQUIRED` if discarded because no readable string symbol was recovered
   - `Single` runtime lifetime reads the evaluated `lifeExp` target at runtime offset `+0x90`, including direct/key/bezier-key source variants
   - `Single` never has more than one active particle
   - `Single` inactive state removes an existing active particle
   - `Single` active state creates a particle only when the active list is empty
   - `Single` loop candidate resets the existing particle age to zero after lifetime instead of spawning or reallocating a replacement
   - `Single` loop fixtures emit `VFX_SINGLE_LOOP_NOT_POC_RESPAWN` if implemented through `loopSingle`/`continuousSingleLoop` dead-particle respawn or a preview `spawnAccumulator`
   - `Single` loop fixtures emit `VFX_SINGLE_LOOP_NOT_BLENDER_EMISSION_RANGE` if Blender `ParticleSettings.count`, `frame_start`, `frame_end`, or `lifetime` creates the loop without preserved Aurora `loop` source provenance
   - `Single` non-positive visible lifetime path clamps negative age to zero and stays diagnostic until retail fixtures prove any later removal/display behavior
   - `Single` fixtures reject a Fountain-with-capacity-one implementation even when the visible particle count matches
12. Render-mode validation:
   - `Normal`, `Billboard_to_Local_Z`, `Billboard_to_World_Z`, `Linked`, `Aligned_to_World_Z`, `Aligned_to_Particle_Dir`, and `Motion_Blur` map to Aurora runtime IDs `0..6`
   - unknown render tokens are preserved and produce diagnostics
   - `Normal` uses the camera/view basis and is not implemented through default Three.js or Blender sprite orientation
   - `Billboard_to_Local_Z` uses the emitter-local orientation basis
   - `Billboard_to_World_Z` uses a fixed/world-Z-style basis and follows the mapped softness-disable gate
   - `Aligned_to_Particle_Dir` uses per-particle orientation/direction basis state
   - `Aligned_to_World_Z` preserves the world-axis height vector path
   - renderer code emits `AuroraParticleBasis` / `AuroraParticleEndpointPair` before choosing Three.js `Sprite`, `BufferGeometry`, `InstancedMesh`, or Blender preview carriers
   - Three.js `Sprite`/`SpriteMaterial` camera-facing billboard output emits `VFX_THREE_SPRITE_BILLBOARD_ADAPTER_ONLY` if used as source truth for any Aurora render mode or if it bypasses `AuroraParticleBasis`
   - Blender particle `Render As` values emit `VFX_BLENDER_PARTICLE_RENDER_AS_ADAPTER_ONLY` if used as canonical `render Normal`, `Linked`, `Billboard_to_*`, `Aligned_*`, or `Motion_Blur` behavior
   - PoC `resolvedBillboard` snapshot labels emit `VFX_POC_BILLBOARD_RESOLVED_DEBUG_PREVIEW_ONLY` when used as proof of Aurora basis math, endpoint topology, or landed/splat orientation
   - `Linked` draws `activeParticleCount - 1` segments and requires a next particle
   - `Linked` with fewer than two active particles produces no textured draw
   - `Linked` preserves active-list adjacency and emits `VFX_LINKED_ACTIVE_LIST_ADJACENCY_REQUIRED` if renderer-side sorting, ring-buffer history, or generated trail points replace `active[i] -> active[i + 1]`
   - PoC-style ring-buffer/trianglestrip previews emit `VFX_POC_LINKED_RING_BUFFER_PREVIEW_ONLY` and `VFX_LINKED_NOT_TRIANGLESTRIP_RING_BUFFER` in canonical mode
   - ordinary textured modes use the same current-position endpoint for both quad centers
   - `Linked` and `Motion_Blur` use endpoint-pair geometry instead of normal billboard geometry
   - `Motion_Blur` requires previous-position state and endpoint color/alpha variation
   - `Motion_Blur` parser fixtures preserve direct/key/bezier-key `blurlength` at target offset `0xcc`
   - `Motion_Blur` constructor/default fixtures initialize missing-token `blurlength` to `1.0f` and copy that offset into runtime/source state
   - `Motion_Blur` source fixtures preserve `opacity` as a profile-gated authoring candidate with local parser-token recovery still unresolved
   - `Motion_Blur` opacity fixtures reject mappings into `alphaStart`/`alphaEnd`, tint alpha, mesh alpha, Three.js material opacity, or CSS opacity
   - `Motion_Blur` update fixtures compute previous-position blending from evaluated `blurlength` as `min(delta, blurlength) / blurlength`, with authored/evaluated non-positive values emitting diagnostics until exact bad-input behavior is proven
   - `Motion_Blur` fixtures reject PoC-style `blurLength * speed` stretching, renderer motion-vector blur, and material/postprocess smear through `VFX_MOTION_BLUR_NOT_BLURLENGTH_SPEED_STRETCH`, `VFX_MOTION_BLUR_NOT_RENDERER_MOTION_VECTOR`, and `VFX_POC_MOTION_BLUR_VELOCITY_STRETCH_PREVIEW_ONLY`
   - PoC opacity/velocity-stretch Motion_Blur previews remain adapter visuals and emit `VFX_POC_MOTION_BLUR_OPACITY_PREVIEW_ONLY` when used as canonical Aurora proof
   - single-quad preview paths emit `VFX_RENDER_MODE_SINGLE_QUAD_PREVIEW_ONLY` when used for `Linked` or `Motion_Blur`
   - `Motion_Blur` validation covers Fountain, Explosion, Single, and Lightning-compatible update timing rather than testing only the final vertex builder
   - local/world-Z and aligned modes do not collapse into one sprite orientation path
   - model propagation fields (`propagaterender`, `propagatecolorshift`, `propagateillumination`, `propagateviewvolume`) remain model/node graph fields and never map to emitter render IDs `0..6`
   - `propagaterender` fixtures preserve raw source/provenance and emit `VFX_MODEL_PROPAGATERENDER_NOT_EMITTER_RENDER` if used as `AuroraMdlEmitterNode.renderMode`
   - `propagateviewvolume` does not become particle emitter culling and emits `VFX_MODEL_PROPAGATE_VIEWVOLUME_NOT_PARTICLE_CULLING` if applied to active/free particle draw gating
   - `propagatecolorshift`/`propagateillumination` do not overwrite particle `colorStart/colorEnd`, `alphaStart/alphaEnd`, tint, or shader uniforms without recovered runtime evidence
   - `wirecolor` remains a base model-node/source-editor color field and does not overwrite particle `colorStart/colorEnd`, `m_isTinted`, light color, material color, or Three.js adapter color without recovered runtime evidence
   - `classification effect/effects` model fixtures preserve model-classification provenance and emit `VFX_MODEL_CLASSIFICATION_EFFECT_NOT_VFX_ROW` when treated as an effect-entry row, programmed-FX request, or emitter update family
   - `setsupermodel` fixtures preserve raw name, resolved chain, unresolved-miss state, and cache-key provenance and emit `VFX_MODEL_SUPERMODEL_CHAIN_PRESERVED` / `VFX_MODEL_SUPERMODEL_NOT_EMITTER_SOURCE` when collapsed into source-emitter fields or preview parent transforms
   - `setanimationscale` and `ignorefog` fixtures stay on the model envelope and emit `VFX_MODEL_ANIMATION_SCALE_NOT_TIMEBASE` or `VFX_MODEL_IGNOREFOG_NOT_PARTICLE_FOG` when mapped to Blender timebase, particle lifetime, effect duration, area fog, material fog, or TXI/MTR fields
   - propagation fixtures record token, source/target node/object, source gate, callback family, and virtual-call evidence; missing records emit `VFX_MODEL_PROPAGATION_EVENT_RECORD_REQUIRED`
   - PoC viewer `visibleByDefault`, `render 0`, shadow-proxy, helper, and bounds policies are preview-only comparison evidence and emit `VFX_POC_VISIBLEBYDEFAULT_NOT_AURORA_PROPAGATION` or `VFX_POC_RENDER_ZERO_POLICY_PREVIEW_ONLY` if used to decide Aurora model propagation
   - landed `splat` particles change basis/size/softness behavior
   - render-mode softness is mode-gated and remains diagnostic until exact uniform naming is proven
   - textured particle renderer builds a contiguous six-vertex buffer per drawn particle/segment
   - textured particle draw uses a non-indexed buffer and reaches the `glDrawArrays` wrapper path; indexed geometry is an adapter optimization only and must preserve Aurora draw provenance
   - the six-vertex textured particle block preserves Aurora's triangle-list-shaped vertex order, including duplicated quad corners at rows `1/4` and `2/3`
   - vertex layout preserves packed color, position, and per-vertex UV fields as separate data
   - atlas frames update per particle through vertex UVs, not a shared material frame offset
   - final `drawModeArg3` / `DAT_00cc996c[3]` enum-table naming remains diagnostic until the graphics wrapper data table is dumped or captured
   - tests may assert the non-indexed draw-array path and triangle-list-shaped six-vertex layout, but they must still emit `VFX_PARTICLE_DRAW_ENUM_TABLE_DUMP_REQUIRED` / `VFX_PARTICLE_DRAW_TRIANGLE_INFERENCE_NOT_ENUM_PROOF` when naming the OpenGL enum from C-export evidence alone
   - Blender `ParticleSettings` reusable-ID imports record all owner object/system references instead of assuming one settings data-block equals one Aurora emitter
   - Missing or unregistered NeverBlender `ParticleSettings.nvb` emits schema diagnostics and does not delete Aurora raw emitter payloads
   - Blender `Action.fcurves` exports are accepted only as first-slot legacy authoring data unless slot/layer/channelbag provenance is resolved
   - Blender `ParticleSettings.render_type` is never used as canonical Aurora render-mode state
13. Blend/render-state validation:
   - `Normal`, `Punch-Through`, and fallback/mode-`2` blend literals map to Aurora runtime buckets without dropping unknown raw tokens
   - `Lighten` is preserved as an author-facing literal but represented as fallback/mode-`2` until retail validation proves the exact equation
   - mode `2` is represented as raw fallback plus optional authoring-name candidate; unknown non-normal/non-punch literals are not silently renamed to `Lighten`
   - mode `0` and mode `2` record the same visible non-punch state sequence in this C export, with exact visual/equation differences capture-gated
   - `Punch-Through` uses the punch-through shader variant path
   - the `blend != 1` shader-variant flag is preserved as a flag, not renamed to `Lighten`, Blender alpha blending, or Three.js additive blending
   - particle textured planes compile/bind the `vsparticle`/`fsparticle` entrypoint pair
   - particle vertex-buffer upload happens before shader variant binding, uniform upload, material-helper application, and draw
   - non-punch and punch-through particle shader variants remain separate cache entries instead of one program controlled only by a material flag
   - particle softness writes float-uniform slot `0` before particle shader binding/draw
   - particle softness is disabled for landed/splat-style candidate state, render modes `1`/`2`, and non-positive max-size candidate
   - particle softness formula preserves `1.0 / min(maxSizeCandidate * 0.2, 0.2)` with the size accumulator name kept diagnostic until fully mapped
   - particle softness input is computed from the max evaluated particle half-extent, not Blender material scale, texture alpha, or arbitrary sprite size
   - Blender material depth/alpha/display settings emit `VFX_BLENDER_MATERIAL_DEPTH_SETTINGS_NOT_PARTICLE_SOFTNESS` if they are used to create or justify `particleSoftness` without Aurora slot-`0` state
   - particle shader variant resolution, softness slot write, shader bind, material helper application, and draw preserve Aurora's local order
   - float-uniform slot `0` writes increment the shader-parameter generation counter and shader activation only uploads changed values for active program locations
   - `particleSoftness` remains a candidate name until shader metadata or runtime capture proves the slot binding
   - `texFBDepth` and `texFBDepthBound` are represented as shader/framebuffer depth-input candidates, not emitter source tokens
   - `texFBDepth`/`texFBDepthBound` preserve texture-unit case `0xc` and bound-flag provenance before any WebGL/Three depth-texture adapter is selected
   - any parsed `EF_DEPTH_TEXTURE`/`0x0800` source bit is profile-gated and preserves raw flag provenance until local parser/runtime proof resolves it
   - `AuroraParticleDepthInputState` records source flag, shader entrypoint, framebuffer-depth resource provenance, capability profile, depth-buffer/viewport provenance, and diagnostics before a browser adapter chooses a depth texture
   - `particleSoftness`, depth-texture sampling, and depth-write mask state remain separate validation lanes
   - Three.js `depthWrite`, `depthTest`, transparent material settings, and PoC preview styles emit `VFX_THREE_DEPTHWRITE_NOT_DEPTH_TEXTURE` or `VFX_POC_DEPTHWRITE_PREVIEW_ONLY` if used as proof of Aurora depth-texture behavior
   - Three.js `DepthTexture` / `WebGLRenderTarget.depthTexture` adapters emit `VFX_THREE_DEPTHTEXTURE_ADAPTER_REQUIRES_AURORA_DEPTH_INPUT` or `VFX_THREE_RENDER_TARGET_DEPTH_NOT_AURORA_SLOT` if created without `AuroraParticleDepthInputState`, texture-unit `0xc` provenance, and `texFBDepthBound` state
   - PoC `ShaderMaterial` payloads without depth-texture/depth-bound uniforms emit `VFX_POC_SHADERMATERIAL_NO_DEPTH_INPUT_PREVIEW_ONLY` if used as soft-particle depth-input proof
   - material helper application runs after particle shader binding and before the draw wrapper, and is represented as an optional material-program rebind/application candidate rather than an emitter `blend` parser substitute
   - draw wrapper mode argument `3` remains an enum-table diagnostic, while non-indexed draw-array routing and vertex count `activeParticleCount * 6` are treated as proven
   - material shader variant selection through `FUN_00a47560` stays separate from emitter `blend` bucket mapping
   - material-lane `additive`/`punchthrough` tokens do not rename or overwrite emitter `Normal`/`Punch-Through`/fallback mode
   - material-lane `sample_framebuffer`, `volumetric`, and custom MTR shaders stay material-lane/rebind candidates and do not replace emitter blend, topology, or particle-update facts
   - scriptable shader uniforms preserve EE/profile, player scope, uniform kind/slot/value, custom shader dependency, shader cache key contribution, and multiplayer reapply policy
   - scriptable shader uniforms emit `VFX_SCRIPTABLE_SHADER_UNIFORM_NOT_EMITTER_FIELD`, `VFX_SCRIPTABLE_SHADER_UNIFORM_NOT_MTR_PARAMETER`, or `VFX_SCRIPTABLE_SHADER_UNIFORM_NOT_PARTICLE_SOFTNESS` if mapped into MDL emitter fields, MTR `parameter`, or the particle softness slot
   - material shader uniform overrides preserve EE/profile, object identity, material name, parameter name, uniform kind/value, reset policy, material-resource owner edge, and shader cache key contribution
   - material shader uniform overrides emit `VFX_MATERIAL_SHADER_UNIFORM_NOT_MTR_PARAMETER`, `VFX_MATERIAL_SHADER_UNIFORM_NOT_SCRIPTABLE_UNIFORM`, `VFX_MATERIAL_SHADER_UNIFORM_NOT_EMITTER_FIELD`, or `VFX_MATERIAL_SHADER_UNIFORM_NOT_PARTICLE_SOFTNESS` if mapped into MTR source defaults, player-global scriptable uniforms, MDL emitter fields, or particle shader softness
   - canonical renderer code emits an `AuroraParticleRenderState` record before choosing any Three.js material or Blender preview material
   - Three.js `transparent`, `depthWrite`, additive blending, or custom blending presets emit adapter-only diagnostics if used as source truth for Aurora blend behavior
   - PoC `Lighten`/`add` to Three.js `AdditiveBlending` mapping emits `VFX_POC_LIGHTEN_ADDITIVE_PREVIEW_ONLY` and cannot satisfy Aurora mode-`2`, blend-equation, depth-write, or draw-order parity
   - PoC alpha scale, size scale, density multiplier, and `deriveAlphaFromColor` formulas derived from `AdditiveBlending` emit `VFX_POC_ADDITIVE_BLEND_SCALES_PREVIEW_ONLY` until an Aurora-owned render-state and particle-evaluation record proves equivalent behavior
   - PoC opaque-additive custom `OneFactor` legacy boost emits `VFX_POC_OPAQUE_ADDITIVE_LEGACY_BOOST_PREVIEW_ONLY` unless retail/GPU capture proves the same blend factors and applicability gates
   - `Punch-Through` enables depth writes while non-punch modes disable depth writes during particle drawing
   - non-punch modes enable the inferred state-`0` transparent lane and disable engine punch-through state `1`
   - punch mode disables the inferred state-`0` transparent lane and enables engine punch-through state `1`
   - the punch-through lane records state `0` disabled, state `1` enabled, and requested depth-write byte enabled before draw
   - the non-punch transparent lane records state `1` disabled, state `0` enabled, requested depth-write byte disabled, and the `FUN_00a7819c` blend-function wrapper invocation
   - state `1` remains an Aurora engine/shader cutout candidate, not proof of fixed-function `GL_ALPHA_TEST`
   - render-state wrappers preserve bitmask-cache behavior, and depth-mask writes stay cached instead of being treated as raw material flags
   - exact `glBlendFunc` source/destination factors remain diagnostic until GPU/retail capture proves them
   - exact `glDepthMask` argument/profile interpretation remains diagnostic where the C export hides GL wrapper arguments
   - local `GL_ARB_*`, `WGL_*`, and `gl*` extension/function-loader strings emit `VFX_GL_EXTENSION_STRING_CAPABILITY_ONLY` / `VFX_GL_FUNCTION_STRING_NOT_VFX_BEHAVIOR` if used as VFX runtime behavior without an Aurora VFX call-site
   - `wglGetProcAddress` evidence emits `VFX_WGL_PROC_ADDRESS_NOT_RUNTIME_CALL` if treated as a particle/beam/material draw call rather than a graphics function loader
   - GL capability discovery cannot replace `AuroraParticleRenderState` and emits `VFX_GL_CAPABILITY_SURFACE_NOT_RENDER_STATE_CONTRACT` when used as blend/depth/render-state proof
   - WebGL/Three capability requirements are adapter facts after Aurora state exists and emit `VFX_WEBGL_ADAPTER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRES_AURORA_STATE` if used as canonical source behavior
   - `twosidedtex` toggles the inferred culling lane without changing the parsed blend literal
   - `twosidedtex` validation preserves source offset `+0x138`, constructor default zero, source clone/import copy, and renderer live-read provenance
   - `twosidedtex` emits `VFX_TWOSIDEDTEX_SOURCE_LIVE_READ_REQUIRED` if copied into a material-only field before the source-node live-read record exists
   - `twosidedtex` emits `VFX_TWOSIDEDTEX_STATE3_CULL_LANE_REQUIRED` if the renderer omits the state-`3` culling/two-sided lane from `AuroraParticleRenderState`
   - Blender material `use_backface_culling`, `show_transparent_back`, and EEVEE backface-culling settings emit `VFX_TWOSIDEDTEX_NOT_BLENDER_BACKFACE_CULLING` when used as source/runtime proof instead of preview-adapter output
14. Render-order validation:
   - parser preserves raw `renderorder` and normalized signed-short value
   - authoring/UI range clamps such as NeverBlender `min=0` stay separate from Aurora runtime range evidence
   - cloned/imported emitter source payload copies the two-byte `renderorder` field
   - draw-item queue includes `renderOrderShort` as an Aurora tie-breaker only after the mapped depth/sort key and referenced-object context
   - `renderorder` emits `VFX_RENDERORDER_NOT_BLEND_DERIVED` if generated from `blend`, `blendMode`, additive/normal material state, or the particle render-state bucket
   - PoC-style `object.renderOrder = blendMode === Additive ? 20 : 10` emits `VFX_POC_RENDERORDER_FROM_BLEND_PREVIEW_ONLY` and never satisfies canonical draw-queue validation
   - current PoC runtime/scene code paths that assign `object.renderOrder` from normalized blend mode emit `VFX_CURRENT_POC_RENDERORDER_BLEND_DERIVED` until replaced by an Aurora draw-queue key in both paths
   - Three.js adapter code emits `VFX_THREE_RENDERORDER_REQUIRES_AURORA_DRAW_QUEUE_RECORD` if it assigns `object.renderOrder` before lane/category, depth key, referenced-object context, and `renderOrderShort` provenance exist
   - lower `renderorder` is treated as a priority candidate, but final direction stays retail-validation-gated
   - Three.js adapter inversion/direction emits `VFX_RENDERORDER_ADAPTER_DIRECTION_PROVENANCE_REQUIRED` until produced from an Aurora draw-queue record with selected profile and retail/capture direction evidence
   - active particles inside one emitter are not camera-sorted unless later evidence proves a specific Aurora mode does so
   - `Linked` preserves active-list adjacency because the next active particle forms the segment endpoint
   - `Motion_Blur` preserves active-list continuity and previous/current particle-position provenance
   - Three.js `Object3D.renderOrder` is used only through an Aurora draw-queue adapter, never as the source contract
   - Blender per-object transparency sorting remains preview behavior and never satisfies Aurora `renderorder` parity by itself
15. P2P validation:
   - missing reference node
   - unresolved reference target
   - `node reference` is parsed and preserved as a first-class model node, including parent node, local transform, animation-track provenance, and source line
   - `node reference` preserves `refModel` and `reattachable` payload fields with local parser provenance, emitting `VFX_MDL_REFERENCE_REFMODEL_PRESERVED` or `VFX_MDL_REFERENCE_REATTACHABLE_PRESERVED` if dropped
   - `refModel` on a reference node does not become emitter `chunkName`, emitter `texture`, VFX phase model, beam body-node, or a synthesized P2P endpoint; misuse emits `VFX_MDL_REFERENCE_REFMODEL_NOT_EMITTER_RESOURCE`
   - P2P target resolution requires a child/reference candidate under the emitter and emits `VFX_P2P_REFERENCE_CHILD_RELATION_REQUIRED` if only a free-floating reference exists
   - multiple child reference candidates preserve candidate order/provenance and emit `VFX_P2P_REFERENCE_MULTIPLE_CANDIDATES_UNVERIFIED` until runtime selection order is proven
   - reference nodes are not resolved through resource lookup and emit `VFX_P2P_REFERENCE_NOT_MODEL_RESOURCE` if treated as an MDL resref
   - UI/Blender target fields, `xsize`/`ysize`, `p2p_bezier2/3`, `src`/`target`, `lightningRadius`, or scene-object selection never synthesize a missing reference node and emit `VFX_P2P_REFERENCE_NOT_UI_TARGET`
   - PoC area selection target modes (`tile`, `placeable`, `door`, `tile_or_placeable_or_door`) emit `VFX_POC_SELECTION_TARGET_NOT_P2P_REFERENCE_NODE` if used as P2P child-reference evidence
   - PoC pick-policy `runtime target` wording for selectable `placeable`/`door` instances emits `VFX_POC_PICK_RUNTIME_TARGET_NOT_LIGHTNING_ENDPOINT` if used as a Lightning/P2P endpoint or runtime pointer replacement
   - PoC walk-player and wing retarget bindings emit `VFX_POC_RETARGET_BINDING_NOT_AURORA_REFERENCE_TARGET` if `Object3D` animation targets are used as Aurora `node reference`, `refModel`, resolver-candidate, or source-target frame evidence
   - reference local transform is evaluated into a runtime world endpoint before Lightning/P2P update and emits `VFX_P2P_REFERENCE_TRANSFORM_RUNTIME_REQUIRED` if omitted
   - evaluated reference world endpoint is recorded explicitly and emits `VFX_P2P_REFERENCE_WORLD_ENDPOINT_REQUIRED` if runtime motion only has emitter-origin data

7. `AuroraVfxResourceRef` + `AuroraVfxDependencyGraph` contract for phase model, texture/TXI/MTR/shader/chunk/sound/spell-slot refs, with parent/child edge provenance, resolver policy trace, PLT gates, custom-shader profile gates, HAK/module precedence diagnostics, phase-sound/audio runtime refs with anchor/profile diagnostics, and chunk MDL/model payload ownership (`emitter.chunkName`, per-particle model ref, release/clear on reuse).
8. A minimal resolver integration path that consumes selected runtime-settings HAK profile data through an explicit VFX source policy or labelled temporary adapter, records `lc_vfx.hak` / `cep3_vfx.hak` provenance when selected, adds runtime-settings revision + HAK-list hash + selected table/resource hash to cache keys, and emits `VFX_INTEGRATION_SOURCE_RESOLVER_MODULE_NOT_READY` / `VFX_INTEGRATION_VFX_SOURCE_POLICY_REQUIRED` if the shared source resolver or VFX source category is not yet implemented.
9. Parser tests using handcrafted 2DA rows and ASCII MDL fixtures, plus explicit regression tests that `parsePlaceablesTwoDaRows()`, GLB `emitter_proxy`, and frontend sprite previews remain non-canonical for VFX runtime.
10. Versioned frontend `AuroraVfxPayload`/`vfxPayload` bridge with diagnostics surfaced through existing preview metadata paths before any canonical browser particle renderer work.
11. Blender adapter contract only after source/runtime payloads exist: import/export keeps `auroraRaw`, `auroraNormalized`, `blenderAuthoring`, and `blenderPreview` separate; the package is versioned, carries `auroraRawHash`, blocks silent export on raw-hash mismatch, runs an explicit export-admission gate for field mapping/unit/timebase/user-intent/profile evidence, and treats NeverBlender split storage, Geometry Nodes bake data, point caches, viewport materials, POC comparison heuristics, and F-Curves as authoring/preview metadata rather than canonical runtime state.

This makes the requested final state more true because every later renderer step will have canonical data, raw fallback, and evidence-driven diagnostics.
